              "patch": "Index: MVP-PLAN.md\n===================================================================\n--- MVP-PLAN.md\t\n+++ MVP-PLAN.md\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,212 @@\n+# Stock Probability MVP Plan\n+\n+## Status And Scope\n+\n+This is the implementation contract for the planned local ARM64 stock probability web app. The repository currently contains only exploratory Python scripts. It does not yet contain the application described below.\n+\n+- `M00` is **Completed** for the four documentation files created in this baseline: `MVP-PLAN.md`, `MVP-ROADMAP.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `README.md`.\n+- `M01` through `M07` are **Pending**. No implementation milestone is complete.\n+- A task may move to **Completed** only after its acceptance evidence, verification result, repair history, and reviewer are recorded.\n+\n+## Product Goal\n+\n+Build a small, auditable, local web application where a user selects a Yahoo Finance stock or ETF and receives two forecast views:\n+\n+1. **Close-to-close:** a forecast from a clearly identified completed market-session close to the applicable next close.\n+2. **Latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close:** a forecast from the latest completed five-minute bar available at request time to the applicable close. An in-progress bar must never be used as completed input.\n+\n+Each view must expose probabilities and magnitude intervals, not just a point estimate. Every displayed result must identify its symbol, asset type, input timestamps, provider/as-of time, forecast horizon, model/version, interval level and units, stale-data state, and any limitation or failure.\n+\n+This is a research and auditability tool, not a trading system or a promise of predictive accuracy.\n+\n+## Non-Negotiable Boundaries\n+\n+### API boundary\n+\n+- All frontend application data must pass through FastAPI `/api/v1`.\n+- The browser must not import a SQLite client, issue SQL, open a database path, or infer storage details from the API.\n+- The API owns validation, provider calls, forecast calculation, persistence, history queries, and backup/restore operations.\n+- API errors must be structured, safe to display, and specific enough to distinguish invalid input, unavailable market data, stale data, calculation failure, persistence failure, and restore failure.\n+\n+### Data source and time semantics\n+\n+- Yahoo Finance is the planned market-data source for user-selected stocks and ETFs.\n+- The provider adapter must record the exact query, requested interval, returned coverage, timezone/session interpretation, response as-of time, and any missing or stale bars.\n+- The forecast service must reject or clearly label insufficient, stale, out-of-session, or ambiguous data. It must not silently substitute a different interval or session.\n+- Close-to-close and five-minute-bar-to-close calculations must have separate, testable horizon semantics. A request made outside market hours must follow a documented session rule rather than an implicit guess.\n+\n+### Persistence and auditability\n+\n+- Every submitted search is an append-only audit event, including successful, failed, and repeated submissions. A repeated search may reuse a valid prior result, but the new submission event must still be stored.\n+- A successful forecast stores an immutable input snapshot: normalized symbol and asset type, request and source timestamps, selected bars, session/calendar interpretation, data-quality flags, model and algorithm version, parameters, thresholds, and provider metadata or content fingerprint.\n+- The immutable result stores probabilities, magnitude intervals, interval levels and units, calculation timestamps, and the input-record reference.\n+- An observed outcome is appended after the forecast horizon with the actual close/return, observation timestamp, comparison rule, and outcome state. It must not rewrite the original forecast input or result.\n+- Corrections require a new versioned record or audit event. No update-in-place behavior may erase what was originally submitted or displayed.\n+- History queries must be bounded, searchable, and served through `/api/v1`; the UI must not scan the database file.\n+\n+### User experience\n+\n+- The dashboard must work at desktop and mobile widths without hiding essential status or controls.\n+- Every search control needs a visible label, keyboard path, focus state, validation message, loading state, empty state, success state, and failure state.\n+- Charts, colors, and interval bands must have text or table equivalents; color alone cannot communicate direction, confidence, stale data, or failure.\n+- History must support practical search/filtering and expose enough context to distinguish a repeated request from a new forecast.\n+- Accessible names, semantic structure, contrast, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and screen-reader announcements are acceptance concerns, not polish.\n+\n+### Deployment and resources\n+\n+- The default service must bind to loopback only. The deployment must make any broader bind an explicit, documented, security-reviewed choice.\n+- Validate symbols, request sizes, date ranges, page sizes, backup paths, and provider timeouts at the API boundary.\n+- Do not expose provider credentials or local file paths to the browser or logs. Avoid unsafe CORS and unbounded concurrent provider calls.\n+- Keep the default process, query, cache, and browser-test footprint suitable for a low-resource ARM64 laptop. Measure rather than assuming that desktop-scale defaults are safe.\n+- All code must have useful comments for non-obvious model, time-window, persistence, security, and resource decisions.\n+\n+## Planned Architecture\n+\n+The intended flow is browser dashboard -> frontend API client -> FastAPI `/api/v1` -> domain services -> Yahoo Finance adapter and server-owned SQLite repositories. The browser has no alternate path to storage or to Yahoo Finance.\n+\n+The API/application layers should remain separable:\n+\n+- **Transport:** FastAPI routes, request/response schemas, validation, safe error mapping, and API versioning.\n+- **Domain:** symbol selection, session/bar semantics, forecast calculation, interval formatting, stale-data policy, and outcome comparison.\n+- **Adapters:** Yahoo Finance retrieval, SQLite repositories/migrations, backup artifact handling, and clock/calendar boundaries.\n+- **Presentation:** responsive accessible dashboard, loading/error/empty states, results, and searchable history.\n+- **Quality:** unit, API, persistence, accessibility, security, performance, restore, and browser regression checks.\n+\n+The exact module names and endpoint names are implementation decisions for M01. The invariants above are not optional.\n+\n+## Forecast Contract\n+\n+The forecast engine must make assumptions visible and reproducible. At minimum, a stored forecast must answer:\n+\n+- Which user-selected symbol and asset type were requested?\n+- Which completed close or five-minute bar was the origin, and which close was the target?\n+- What market timezone, trading-session rule, and provider response were used?\n+- What historical window, features, parameters, thresholds, and model/version produced the output?\n+- What probability definitions were used, such as direction or return threshold?\n+- What do the magnitude intervals mean, what confidence/coverage level do they represent, and are they expressed as percent return, price, or both?\n+- What data was missing, stale, unavailable, or outside the supported market session?\n+\n+The current hard-coded and dummy calculations are not acceptance evidence for this contract. M03 must replace or explicitly isolate them behind tested, versioned domain behavior and must not present mock backtests as validated forecasts.\n+\n+## Task Register\n+\n+The coordinator assigns no more than three agents to a task in addition to the coordinator. The listed acceptance evidence is required before status can become **Completed**.\n+\n+### M00 - Documentation Baseline\n+\n+- **Status:** Completed, docs only.\n+- **Dependencies:** None.\n+- **Agents:** `LUNA MAX docs`.\n+- **Scope:** Create the plan, roadmap, compact agent rules, and honest repository README.\n+- **Acceptance evidence:** [x] `MVP-PLAN.md`, `MVP-ROADMAP.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `README.md` exist; [x] current prototype is distinguished from planned implementation; [x] implementation milestones remain pending.\n+- **Verification:** [x] documentation-only diff reviewed; [x] required product invariants, orchestration, evidence fields, repair loop, and final definition of done are present.\n+- **Repair record:** None at baseline creation.\n+\n+### M01 - API And Application Shell\n+\n+- **Status:** Pending.\n+- **Dependencies:** M00.\n+- **Agents:** `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\n+- **Scope:** Establish the ARM64-friendly application layout, FastAPI service, versioned `/api/v1` boundary, structured errors, health/readiness behavior, frontend shell, and documented local loopback launch path.\n+- **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] API contract and schema tests pass; [ ] a browser can obtain application data only through `/api/v1`; [ ] no frontend source imports a database driver or opens a SQLite path; [ ] loopback smoke test passes on the target ARM64 environment; [ ] non-obvious code decisions have useful comments.\n+- **Verification:** [ ] unit and API tests; [ ] negative validation tests; [ ] browser network inspection; [ ] local ARM64 startup and bounded-resource smoke test.\n+- **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M01-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\n+\n+### M02 - SQLite Audit And Immutable Records\n+\n+- **Status:** Pending.\n+- **Dependencies:** M01.\n+- **Agents:** `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\n+- **Scope:** Define migrations and repositories for search events, successful/failed/repeated status, immutable forecast inputs, immutable results, append-only outcomes, provenance, and bounded searchable history.\n+- **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] migration is reproducible on a clean database; [ ] every submission persists exactly one auditable event even on failure or repetition; [ ] input, result, and outcome records cannot be silently overwritten; [ ] history filters and pagination work through `/api/v1`; [ ] restart preserves records.\n+- **Verification:** [ ] repository and migration tests; [ ] success/failure/repeat matrix; [ ] immutability and concurrent-write tests; [ ] API authorization/boundary test showing no direct browser database access.\n+- **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M02-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\n+\n+### M03 - Yahoo Finance Data And Forecast Engine\n+\n+- **Status:** Pending.\n+- **Dependencies:** M01 and M02.\n+- **Agents:** `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\n+- **Scope:** Implement the provider adapter, symbol/asset validation, completed-bar selection, close-to-close and latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close horizons, probability calculations, magnitude intervals, provenance, stale/missing-data handling, and immutable forecast writes.\n+- **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] stock and ETF selections follow one tested contract; [ ] an in-progress five-minute bar is excluded; [ ] both horizons identify their origin and target timestamps; [ ] probabilities and magnitude intervals include definitions, levels, units, and model/version; [ ] provider failures and insufficient data create auditable failed searches without fabricated results; [ ] deterministic fixtures reproduce recorded outputs.\n+- **Verification:** [ ] provider adapter tests with fixtures; [ ] timezone/session and boundary-time tests; [ ] incomplete-bar, missing-bar, stale-data, and out-of-session tests; [ ] numerical invariants and repeatability checks; [ ] ARM64 resource smoke test.\n+- **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M03-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\n+\n+### M04 - Dashboard And Searchable History\n+\n+- **Status:** Pending.\n+- **Dependencies:** M01, M02, and M03.\n+- **Agents:** `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\n+- **Scope:** Build the responsive accessible dashboard for symbol selection, forecast submission, result comparison, source/as-of/stale/error context, and searchable history.\n+- **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] desktop and mobile layouts retain all essential content; [ ] keyboard and screen-reader flows cover search, results, errors, and history; [ ] loading, empty, failed, repeated, stale, and successful states are understandable without color; [ ] result views show both forecast modes, probabilities, and magnitude intervals; [ ] all data requests use `/api/v1`.\n+- **Verification:** [ ] component and API integration tests; [ ] accessibility audit and keyboard pass; [ ] checked-in browser regression scenarios; [ ] browser network assertion for the API-only boundary; [ ] low-resource render smoke test.\n+- **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M04-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\n+\n+### M05 - Backup, Restore, And Secure Loopback Operations\n+\n+- **Status:** Pending.\n+- **Dependencies:** M02 and M04.\n+- **Agents:** `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\n+- **Scope:** Add verified backup and restore workflow, integrity/manifest checks, safe restore staging, loopback deployment defaults, input/path validation, timeout limits, and operational documentation.\n+- **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] a backup includes the required SQLite data and verifiable metadata/checksum; [ ] restore to a clean or staging location validates schema, integrity, and representative counts before promotion; [ ] a tampered, truncated, incompatible, or unsafe-path artifact is rejected; [ ] active data is not silently destroyed; [ ] default bind is loopback and security behavior is documented.\n+- **Verification:** [ ] backup/restore round trip; [ ] negative artifact and path tests; [ ] restart and recovery test; [ ] loopback exposure check; [ ] resource and timeout checks on ARM64.\n+- **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M05-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\n+\n+### M06 - QA, Playwright MCP, Browser Regressions, And CI\n+\n+- **Status:** Pending.\n+- **Dependencies:** M01, M02, M03, M04, and M05.\n+- **Agents:** `LUNA MAX QA`, `SOL HIGH build`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\n+- **Scope:** Configure the official `@playwright/mcp` headless for agent QA, check in automated browser regressions, and establish Git/CI gates for linting, typing or static checks where adopted, unit/API tests, accessibility, security, resource limits, migration, and backup/restore.\n+- **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] the official MCP configuration is discoverable and runs headless; [ ] browser regressions are checked in and run against a deterministic local app; [ ] CI blocks a failing unit/API/browser/accessibility/security/restore gate; [ ] test artifacts identify task and commit context; [ ] no test depends on the tracked `burry_env/` or local `.venv/`.\n+- **Verification:** [ ] clean-environment CI run; [ ] intentional-failure gate test; [ ] headless MCP smoke run; [ ] browser regression run on desktop and mobile viewports; [ ] ARM64 or documented equivalent resource run.\n+- **Repair record:** Record each failed check as `R-M06-<n>` with failing evidence and rerun result.\n+\n+### M07 - Integrated MVP Acceptance\n+\n+- **Status:** Pending.\n+- **Dependencies:** M06.\n+- **Agents:** `LUNA MAX QA`, `LUNA MAX docs`.\n+- **Scope:** Run the complete user journey and release review on a low-resource ARM64 laptop, reconcile all task evidence, and publish the supported local operation and limitations.\n+- **Acceptance evidence:** [ ] a user selects a stock and an ETF and receives both forecast horizons; [ ] probabilities and magnitude intervals are traceable to immutable inputs/results; [ ] successful, failed, and repeated searches appear in searchable history; [ ] outcomes can be appended without changing forecasts; [ ] backup/restore is verified; [ ] responsive/accessibility, loopback security, MCP/browser, comments, and Git/CI gates all pass; [ ] README and roadmap state the shipped scope honestly.\n+- **Verification:** [ ] full CI; [ ] end-to-end browser journey; [ ] restore from the produced artifact; [ ] security and accessibility sign-off; [ ] performance/resource evidence; [ ] coordinator review of every dependency and evidence field.\n+- **Repair record:** Record each failed release check as `R-M07-<n>` and keep M07 pending until repaired and rerun.\n+\n+## Evidence Record Format\n+\n+Every implementation task must maintain these fields in its task record or linked review:\n+\n+- **Task ID:** the exact `M##` or `R-M##-<n>` identifier.\n+- **Status:** `Pending`, `In progress`, `Blocked`, or `Completed`.\n+- **Dependencies verified:** the completed task IDs and evidence references.\n+- **Change summary:** what changed and what did not change.\n+- **Acceptance evidence:** links, test names, fixture IDs, screenshots, logs, checksums, or measured resource results.\n+- **Verification result:** command/check name, environment, timestamp, and pass/fail result.\n+- **Repair history:** each failure, root cause, repair, and rerun result; use `None` only when no repair was needed.\n+- **Reviewer:** the coordinator and the verifying agent.\n+\n+Evidence is not a prose promise. A skipped or unavailable check must be recorded as such and cannot satisfy a required acceptance field.\n+\n+## Verification And Repair Loop\n+\n+1. The coordinator selects the next pending task only after its dependencies have completed with evidence.\n+2. The assigned build, QA, and documentation agents work within the task scope and keep the task status visible.\n+3. The coordinator runs the targeted verification set, then the applicable repository/Git/CI gates.\n+4. If any check fails, the task remains pending or in progress. The coordinator records the failure, creates `R-M##-<n>`, assigns no more than three agents, and repairs the root cause rather than weakening the check.\n+5. QA reruns the failed check and the relevant regression set. Documentation records the new evidence and any limitation.\n+6. The coordinator marks the task completed only when every required acceptance field passes and the reviewer is named.\n+\n+## Final Definition Of Done\n+\n+The MVP is done only when all of the following are true:\n+\n+- M00 through M07 have explicit statuses and evidence, with no implementation milestone marked complete by assertion alone.\n+- A user can select Yahoo Finance stocks and ETFs and receive close-to-close and latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close forecasts with clear session/bar semantics.\n+- Results contain probabilities and defined magnitude intervals with source, as-of, stale/error, model/version, input, and output provenance.\n+- Every submitted successful, failed, and repeated search is retained, history is searchable through `/api/v1`, and forecast inputs/results/outcomes are immutable or append-only as specified.\n+- Backup artifacts and restores are verified through integrity, compatibility, representative-data, and non-destructive promotion checks.\n+- The frontend uses FastAPI `/api/v1` for all application data and has no direct SQLite access.\n+- The dashboard is responsive and accessible, including keyboard, screen-reader, text-equivalent, loading, empty, stale, repeated, and failure behavior.\n+- The default deployment is secure loopback, bounded for a low-resource ARM64 laptop, and documented with its limitations.\n+- The official headless `@playwright/mcp` supports agent QA, automated browser regressions are checked in, and Git/CI gates fail closed on required regressions.\n+- Code comments explain non-obvious behavior, the supported local workflow is documented, and README claims match the evidence actually shipped.\n",

              "patch": "Index: MVP-ROADMAP.md\n===================================================================\n--- MVP-ROADMAP.md\t\n+++ MVP-ROADMAP.md\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,95 @@\n+# Stock Probability MVP Roadmap\n+\n+## Status Snapshot\n+\n+This roadmap tracks delivery of the planned local ARM64 stock probability web app. The current repository is still an exploratory Python prototype.\n+\n+- **Completed:** `M00` documentation baseline only. The four requested docs were created: `MVP-PLAN.md`, `MVP-ROADMAP.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `README.md`.\n+- **Pending:** every implementation milestone, `M01` through `M07`.\n+- **Rule:** status cannot advance without the acceptance evidence and verification record defined in `MVP-PLAN.md`.\n+\n+## Dependency-Ordered Milestones\n+\n+| ID | Milestone | Dependencies | Status | Acceptance evidence required |\n+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n+| M00 | Documentation baseline | None | Completed, docs only | Four docs exist; prototype and planned app are separated; implementation remains pending. |\n+| M01 | API and application shell | M00 | Pending | FastAPI `/api/v1`, structured errors, frontend shell, loopback smoke test, and no frontend database access. |\n+| M02 | SQLite audit and immutable records | M01 | Pending | Successful, failed, and repeated submissions persist; immutable inputs/results; append-only outcomes; searchable API history. |\n+| M03 | Yahoo Finance data and forecast engine | M01, M02 | Pending | Stock/ETF selection; close-to-close and latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close; probabilities; defined magnitude intervals; stale/error handling. |\n+| M04 | Dashboard and searchable history | M01, M02, M03 | Pending | Responsive accessible UI, full state coverage, both forecast views, and API-only application data. |\n+| M05 | Backup, restore, and secure loopback operations | M02, M04 | Pending | Verified integrity/restore round trip, rejected unsafe artifacts, safe promotion, loopback default, and bounded operations. |\n+| M06 | QA, MCP, browser regressions, and CI | M01, M02, M03, M04, M05 | Pending | Official headless `@playwright/mcp`, checked-in browser regressions, Git/CI gates, and ARM64 resource evidence. |\n+| M07 | Integrated MVP acceptance | M06 | Pending | Complete user journey, audit/history/outcome proof, restore proof, accessibility/security/QA sign-off, and honest release docs. |\n+\n+## Delivery Phases\n+\n+### Phase 0: Establish The Contract\n+\n+`M00` is complete for documentation only. The plan defines the API/storage boundary, time semantics, evidence format, verification/repair loop, and final definition of done. It does not mean that any application behavior exists.\n+\n+### Phase 1: Make The Boundary Real\n+\n+`M01` creates the smallest runnable application shape. `M02` makes search activity and forecast records durable. Do not build a UI that bypasses the API, and do not call a database schema complete without failure and repeat cases.\n+\n+### Phase 2: Make Forecasts Traceable\n+\n+`M03` integrates Yahoo Finance through a server-side adapter and separates the two forecast horizons. The key gate is not a plausible number; it is reproducibility from captured completed bars, explicit session rules, model/version, probabilities, intervals, and data-quality state.\n+\n+### Phase 3: Make The Workflow Usable\n+\n+`M04` turns the API into a responsive accessible dashboard and searchable history view. Loading, empty, failure, stale, repeated, and success states are part of the feature. All frontend application data continues to use FastAPI `/api/v1`.\n+\n+### Phase 4: Make Local Operation Durable\n+\n+`M05` adds verified backups/restores and secure loopback defaults. A restore is not accepted because a file exists; it must pass integrity, compatibility, representative-data, and non-destructive promotion checks.\n+\n+### Phase 5: Make Regressions Visible\n+\n+`M06` configures the official `@playwright/mcp` headless for agent QA, checks browser regressions into the repository, and makes Git/CI gates enforce the contract. The test environment must not depend on `burry_env/` or the local `.venv/`.\n+\n+### Phase 6: Release Only With Evidence\n+\n+`M07` exercises the full workflow on a low-resource ARM64 laptop and reconciles every acceptance field. A missing provider result, skipped accessibility check, unverified restore, direct database path, or undocumented limitation keeps the release pending.\n+\n+## Ownership Model\n+\n+- The **coordinator** owns task assignment, dependency checks, integration, status, evidence, and release decisions.\n+- **SOL HIGH build** owns application implementation, API/storage/provider/UI changes, and targeted engineering fixes.\n+- **LUNA MAX QA** owns unit/API/browser/accessibility/security/performance/restore verification and regression evidence.\n+- **LUNA MAX docs** owns this roadmap, the detailed plan, runbooks, evidence records, and honest status wording.\n+- Each task uses the coordinator plus no more than three agents. Agents must work from the explicit task ID and may not silently expand scope.\n+\n+## Gates And Repair Loop\n+\n+The coordinator uses the following loop for every milestone:\n+\n+1. Confirm all dependency IDs are completed with evidence.\n+2. Assign up to three agents and record the task's change summary and acceptance fields.\n+3. Run targeted checks, then the relevant Git/CI gates.\n+4. On failure, leave the task pending or in progress, record the failed evidence, create a repair ID such as `R-M03-1`, and fix the root cause.\n+5. Rerun the failed check plus the affected regression set. Record the environment, result, and reviewer.\n+6. Mark completed only when all required evidence passes; never replace missing evidence with a narrative status update.\n+\n+## Roadmap Completion Record\n+\n+Use this record when a milestone is reviewed. It is intentionally blank for implementation work until that work occurs.\n+\n+- **Task ID:** `M##`.\n+- **Dependencies verified:** task IDs and evidence references.\n+- **Status:** `Pending`, `In progress`, `Blocked`, or `Completed`.\n+- **Acceptance evidence:** test names, logs, screenshots, fixtures, checksums, or measured resource results.\n+- **Verification result:** environment, check, timestamp, and pass/fail.\n+- **Repair history:** repair IDs, root causes, fixes, and reruns.\n+- **Reviewer:** coordinator plus verifying agent.\n+\n+## Release Definition Of Done\n+\n+The roadmap is complete only when `M00` through `M07` are accounted for and the planned app can demonstrate all of these outcomes:\n+\n+- User-selected Yahoo Finance stocks and ETFs support both forecast horizons, with the latest five-minute input always a completed bar.\n+- Probabilities and magnitude intervals have explicit definitions, levels, units, timestamps, source, model/version, and data-quality context.\n+- SQLite retains every successful, failed, and repeated search and immutable forecast inputs/results with append-only outcomes.\n+- Searchable history and verified backup/restore work through the FastAPI boundary; the frontend never accesses SQLite directly.\n+- The dashboard is responsive and accessible, and the default deployment is secure loopback with bounded ARM64 resource use.\n+- The official headless `@playwright/mcp`, checked-in browser regressions, useful code comments, and Git/CI gates are present and passing.\n+- README, plan, and roadmap describe only behavior supported by the final evidence.\n",

              "patch": "Index: README.md\n===================================================================\n--- README.md\t\n+++ README.md\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,41 @@\n+# Stock Probability\n+\n+## Status\n+\n+This repository is an early, documentation-led prototype. The planned local ARM64 web application is **not implemented yet**.\n+\n+The current tracked application material is limited to exploratory Python scripts:\n+\n+- `prob_calc.py` contains an interactive blended-probability experiment with hard-coded scenarios, sample weights, and a dummy backtest.\n+- `prob_calc_hardcoded.py` contains a similar hard-coded experiment.\n+- `prob_calc_yf.py` is an unfinished Yahoo Finance daily-data experiment, not a supported web endpoint or production forecast engine.\n+\n+There is currently no FastAPI service, frontend dashboard, SQLite application schema, searchable history, backup/restore workflow, automated browser regression suite, Playwright MCP configuration, dependency manifest, or CI release gate. The scripts and local environments must not be presented as those features.\n+\n+## Planned MVP\n+\n+The MVP will be a local, loopback-only web app for selecting Yahoo Finance stocks and ETFs and reviewing probability forecasts. It will run on an ARM64 laptop with bounded resource use and will show:\n+\n+- A close-to-close forecast based on clearly recorded completed-session timestamps.\n+- A latest-completed-5-minute-bar-to-close forecast that never treats an in-progress bar as completed.\n+- Direction or threshold probabilities alongside magnitude intervals that state their level, units, as-of time, and data quality.\n+- Source, model/version, stale-data, market-session, and error context so a result is auditable rather than an unexplained number.\n+- Searchable history, including every submitted successful, failed, and repeated search.\n+\n+The application boundary is strict: the browser will obtain all application data through FastAPI `/api/v1`. It will never open SQLite, issue SQL, or access a database file directly. SQLite will be server-owned and will retain immutable forecast input snapshots, results, and later observed outcomes.\n+\n+The dashboard is planned to be responsive and accessible on desktop and mobile layouts. The deployment is planned to bind to loopback by default, validate inputs, avoid exposing secrets, and make provider failures visible. Verified backup and restore, useful comments in all code, Git/CI gates, the official headless `@playwright/mcp` setup for agent QA, and checked-in automated browser regressions are release requirements.\n+\n+These are plans, not current capabilities. Forecasts are informational research outputs, not investment advice or a guarantee of future prices.\n+\n+## Documentation Map\n+\n+- `MVP-PLAN.md` is the detailed contract, architecture direction, task register, evidence format, and definition of done.\n+- `MVP-ROADMAP.md` is the dependency-ordered delivery view and status board.\n+- `AGENTS.md` contains compact operating rules for implementation, QA, documentation, and repository hygiene.\n+\n+## Current Development Guidance\n+\n+No supported installation or launch command is published yet because the application structure and dependency manifest do not exist. Treat the prototype scripts as historical experiments and inspect their source before relying on any calculation. Do not use `burry_env/` as a source of truth; it is tracked legacy dependency noise. `.venv/` is local environment state.\n+\n+The next implementation work starts at M01 in the plan. M00 is complete only for the four documentation files created with this baseline; all implementation milestones remain pending.\n",

              "file": "Makefile",
              "patch": "Index: Makefile\n===================================================================\n--- Makefile\t\n+++ Makefile\t\n@@ -1,68 +1,84 @@\n # All commands use an isolated development environment, never tracked burry_env or local .venv.\n+# Pinned local toolchains avoid accidentally using tracked burry_env or a developer's .venv.\n PYTHON := .dev-venv/bin/python\n PIP := .dev-venv/bin/pip\n NODE_BIN := .tools/node/bin\n NPM := $(NODE_BIN)/npm\n NPX := $(NODE_BIN)/npx\n \n-.PHONY: setup dev migrate test lint static check browser-setup browser-install browser-test mcp-smoke acceptance live live-smoke release release-check backup restore clean\n+.PHONY: setup dev migrate test lint typecheck static security restore-test check browser-setup browser-install browser-test mcp-smoke acceptance live live-smoke release release-check backup restore clean\n \n setup:\n \tpython3 -m venv .dev-venv\n-\t$(PIP) install --requirement requirements.lock\n-\t$(PIP) install --no-deps --editable .\n+\t$(PYTHON) -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check pip==25.2\n+\t$(PIP) install --disable-pip-version-check --requirement requirements.lock\n+\t$(PIP) install --disable-pip-version-check --no-build-isolation --no-deps --editable .\n \n dev:\n \t$(PYTHON) -m stock_probs.cli serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000\n \n migrate:\n \t$(PYTHON) -m stock_probs.cli migrate\n \n test:\n-\t$(PYTHON) -m pytest -m \"not live\" --cov=stock_probs --cov-report=term-missing\n+\tmkdir -p test-results/python\n+\t$(PYTHON) -m pytest -m \"not live\" --cov=stock_probs --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=85 --junitxml=test-results/python/junit.xml\n \n lint:\n \t$(PYTHON) -m ruff check src tests scripts\n \n+typecheck:\n+\t# M05 operational modules are the first strict typing boundary; imported app layers stay separate.\n+\t$(PYTHON) -m mypy src/stock_probs/backup.py src/stock_probs/cli.py\n+\n static:\n \t$(PYTHON) -m compileall -q src tests scripts\n \tbash -n scripts/*.sh\n \t$(PYTHON) scripts/comment_audit.py\n \n-check: lint static test\n+security:\n+\t# Ruff's S rules fail here; the non-live suite above supplies host/origin/path regressions.\n+\t$(PYTHON) -m ruff check --select S --ignore S101 src tests scripts\n \n+restore-test:\n+\t$(PYTHON) -m pytest tests/test_repository_backup.py tests/test_backup_cli.py -q\n+\n+check: lint typecheck static test security restore-test\n+\n browser-setup:\n \t./scripts/install-node-arm64.sh\n \tPATH=\"$(CURDIR)/$(NODE_BIN):$$PATH\" $(NPM) --prefix tools/browser ci\n \n browser-install: browser-setup\n \t# Playwright's maintained dependency list is architecture-aware on supported Linux hosts.\n \tPATH=\"$(CURDIR)/$(NODE_BIN):$$PATH\" $(NPX) --prefix tools/browser playwright install --with-deps chromium\n \n-browser-test:\n+browser-test: browser-setup\n \tPATH=\"$(CURDIR)/$(NODE_BIN):$$PATH\" $(NPM) --prefix tools/browser test\n \n-mcp-smoke:\n-\t./scripts/playwright-mcp.sh --version\n+mcp-smoke: browser-setup\n+\t# The smoke client initializes MCP, lists tools, and opens an isolated Chromium context.\n+\tPATH=\"$(CURDIR)/$(NODE_BIN):$$PATH\" $(NODE_BIN)/node tools/browser/mcp-smoke.js\n \n acceptance: check browser-test\n \n live-smoke:\n \t$(PYTHON) -m pytest -m live -v\n \n live: live-smoke\n \n release-check: acceptance\n \t$(PYTHON) -m stock_probs.cli migrate\n+\t$(PYTHON) -m pytest tests/test_backup_cli.py -q\n \n release: release-check\n \n backup:\n \t$(PYTHON) -m stock_probs.cli backup\n \n # Usage: make restore BACKUP=stock-probs-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ.spbackup PROMOTE=--promote\n restore:\n \t$(PYTHON) -m stock_probs.cli restore \"$(BACKUP)\" $(PROMOTE)\n \n clean:\n-\trm -rf .pytest_cache .ruff_cache test-results playwright-report .playwright-mcp\n+\trm -rf .pytest_cache .ruff_cache test-results playwright-report .playwright-mcp tools/browser/test-results tools/browser/playwright-report\n",
              "additions": 25,
              "deletions": 9,
              "status": "modified"
            },
            {
              "file": "opencode.json",
              "patch": "Index: opencode.json\n===================================================================\n--- opencode.json\t\n+++ opencode.json\t\n@@ -1,13 +1,37 @@\n {\n-  // The official pinned MCP wrapper always adds headless and isolated browser flags.\n   \"$schema\": \"https://opencode.ai/config.json\",\n   \"instructions\": [\"AGENTS.md\"],\n   \"mcp\": {\n     \"playwright\": {\n       \"type\": \"local\",\n-      \"command\": [\"./scripts/playwright-mcp.sh\"],\n+      \"command\": [\n+        \"./scripts/playwright-mcp.sh\",\n+        \"--headless\",\n+        \"--isolated\",\n+        \"--browser\",\n+        \"chromium\",\n+        \"--allowed-hosts\",\n+        \"127.0.0.1,localhost,[::1]\",\n+        \"--allowed-origins\",\n+        \"http://127.0.0.1:*;http://localhost:*;http://[::1]:8000;http://[::1]:8765\",\n+        \"--block-service-workers\",\n+        \"--image-responses\",\n+        \"omit\",\n+        \"--output-dir\",\n+        \".playwright-mcp\",\n+        \"--output-max-size\",\n+        \"10485760\",\n+        \"--timeout-action\",\n+        \"10000\",\n+        \"--timeout-navigation\",\n+        \"30000\"\n+      ],\n       \"enabled\": true,\n       \"timeout\": 30000\n     }\n+  },\n+  \"tool_output\": {\n+    \"max_lines\": 500,\n+    \"max_bytes\": 32768\n   }\n }\n",
              "additions": 26,
              "deletions": 2,
              "status": "modified"
            },
            {
              "file": "pyproject.toml",
              "patch": "Index: pyproject.toml\n===================================================================\n--- pyproject.toml\t\n+++ pyproject.toml\t\n@@ -1,50 +1,57 @@\n # Exact direct versions plus the checked-in transitive lock make ARM64 setup reproducible.\n [build-system]\n requires = [\"setuptools==80.9.0\"]\n build-backend = \"setuptools.build_meta\"\n \n [project]\n name = \"stock-probs\"\n version = \"0.1.0\"\n description = \"Auditable local stock probability forecasts\"\n requires-python = \">=3.11\"\n dependencies = [\n   \"fastapi==0.116.1\",\n   \"uvicorn==0.35.0\",\n   \"yfinance==1.7.0\",\n ]\n \n [project.optional-dependencies]\n dev = [\n   \"httpx==0.28.1\",\n+  \"mypy==1.17.1\",\n   \"pytest==8.4.1\",\n   \"pytest-cov==6.2.1\",\n   \"ruff==0.12.9\",\n ]\n \n [project.scripts]\n stock-probs = \"stock_probs.cli:main\"\n \n [tool.setuptools]\n package-dir = {\"\" = \"src\"}\n \n [tool.setuptools.packages.find]\n where = [\"src\"]\n \n [tool.setuptools.package-data]\n # The server owns these static assets so their only data client remains /api/v1.\n stock_probs = [\"static/*\", \"migrations/*.sql\", \"fixtures/*.json\"]\n \n [tool.pytest.ini_options]\n addopts = \"-q --strict-markers --disable-warnings\"\n testpaths = [\"tests\"]\n markers = [\"live: requires Yahoo network access and is excluded from deterministic gates\"]\n \n+[tool.mypy]\n+# M05 starts strict typing at the backup/CLI boundary without masking debt in other owned layers.\n+python_version = \"3.11\"\n+strict = true\n+show_error_codes = true\n+\n [tool.ruff]\n line-length = 100\n target-version = \"py311\"\n exclude = [\"burry_env\", \".venv\", \".dev-venv\"]\n \n [tool.ruff.lint]\n select = [\"E\", \"F\", \"I\", \"B\", \"UP\", \"S\", \"SIM\"]\n ignore = [\"S101\"] # Assertions are intentional in tests and domain invariants.\n",
              "additions": 7,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "modified"

              "file": "scripts/install-node-arm64.sh",
              "patch": "Index: scripts/install-node-arm64.sh\n===================================================================\n--- scripts/install-node-arm64.sh\t\n+++ scripts/install-node-arm64.sh\t\n@@ -1,30 +1,40 @@\n #!/usr/bin/env bash\n-# Install a pinned official Node archive locally and verify it before extraction.\n+# Install a pinned official Node archive locally after checking an embedded release checksum.\n set -euo pipefail\n \n NODE_VERSION=\"22.19.0\"\n ARCH=\"$(uname -m)\"\n case \"$ARCH\" in\n-  aarch64|arm64) NODE_ARCH=\"arm64\" ;;\n-  x86_64|amd64) NODE_ARCH=\"x64\" ;;\n-  *) echo \"Unsupported Node architecture: $ARCH\" >&2; exit 2 ;;\n+  aarch64|arm64)\n+    NODE_ARCH=\"arm64\"\n+    NODE_SHA256=\"0b2d9f564b6594222a62c82e1df2efe119dd4a4aff29644f4dd325bf360b6bcc\"\n+    ;;\n+  x86_64|amd64)\n+    NODE_ARCH=\"x64\"\n+    NODE_SHA256=\"c0649af18e6a24f6fe5535a3e86b341dd49a8e71117c8b68bde973ef834f16f2\"\n+    ;;\n+  *) printf 'Unsupported Node architecture: %s\\n' \"$ARCH\" >&2; exit 2 ;;\n esac\n \n ROOT=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")/..\" && pwd)\"\n INSTALL_DIR=\"$ROOT/.tools/node\"\n if [[ -x \"$INSTALL_DIR/bin/node\" ]]; then\n-  \"$INSTALL_DIR/bin/node\" --version\n-  exit 0\n+  if [[ \"$(\"$INSTALL_DIR/bin/node\" --version)\" == \"v${NODE_VERSION}\" ]]; then\n+    \"$INSTALL_DIR/bin/node\" --version\n+    exit 0\n+  fi\n+  printf 'Existing local Node is not v%s; remove .tools/node before setup.\\n' \"$NODE_VERSION\" >&2\n+  exit 2\n fi\n \n TMP_DIR=\"$(mktemp -d)\"\n trap 'rm -rf \"$TMP_DIR\"' EXIT\n ARCHIVE=\"node-v${NODE_VERSION}-linux-${NODE_ARCH}.tar.xz\"\n BASE_URL=\"https://nodejs.org/dist/v${NODE_VERSION}\"\n-curl --fail --location --retry 3 --output \"$TMP_DIR/$ARCHIVE\" \"$BASE_URL/$ARCHIVE\"\n-curl --fail --location --retry 3 --output \"$TMP_DIR/SHASUMS256.txt\" \"$BASE_URL/SHASUMS256.txt\"\n-(cd \"$TMP_DIR\" && grep \"  $ARCHIVE\\$\" SHASUMS256.txt | sha256sum --check --strict -)\n+curl --fail --location --retry 3 --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 \\\n+  --output \"$TMP_DIR/$ARCHIVE\" \"$BASE_URL/$ARCHIVE\"\n+printf '%s  %s\\n' \"$NODE_SHA256\" \"$TMP_DIR/$ARCHIVE\" | sha256sum --check --strict -\n mkdir -p \"$ROOT/.tools\"\n tar -xJf \"$TMP_DIR/$ARCHIVE\" -C \"$TMP_DIR\"\n mv \"$TMP_DIR/node-v${NODE_VERSION}-linux-${NODE_ARCH}\" \"$INSTALL_DIR\"\n \"$INSTALL_DIR/bin/node\" --version\n",

run_id INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES forecast_runs(id),\n     snapshot_json TEXT NOT NULL,\n     created_at TEXT NOT NULL\n );\n \n CREATE TABLE forecast_results (\n     id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n     input_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES forecast_inputs(id),\n     horizon TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (horizon IN ('close_to_close', 'completed_5m_to_close')),\n     result_json TEXT NOT search_events BEGIN\n     SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'search_events are append-only');\n END;\n CREATE TRIGGER immutable_search_events_delete BEFORE DELETE ON search_events BEGIN\n     SELECT RAISE(ABORT, staging.cleanup()\n+\n+\n+def test_restore_rejects_self_consistent_but_incompatible_schema(settings):\n+    _, manager = _manager(settings)\n+    source = settings.backup_dir /      staged.write_bytes(database)\n+        with sqlite3.connect(staged) as connection:\n+            connection.execute(\"CREATE TABLE incompatible_extension(value TEXT)\")\n+        changed = staged.read_bytes()\n+        staged.unlink()\n+        manifest[\"database_sha256\"] = hashlib.sha256(changed).hexdigest()\n+        manifest[\"database_size\"] = len(changed)\n+        # Matching \n \n def test_restore_rejects_tampering_and_unsafe_names(settings):\n     repository, service = _service(settings)\n     service.search(\"ACDC\", \"stock\")\n     manager = BackupManager(repository, Twenty immutable snapshots cover a useful burst without desktop-scale memory or disk use.\n     assert peak < 64 * 1024 * 1024\n     assert settings.database_path.stat().st_size < 16 * 1024 * 1024\n     assert repository.history(page_size=100)[\"total\"] == 20\n+\n+\n+def test_dashboard_and_price_slice_stay_lightweight(client):\n+    # The shell has no framework bundle, and chart consumers can request a tiny captured slice.\n+    asset_bytes = sum(\n+        len(client.get(path).content)\n+        for path in (\"/\", \"/assets/app.css\", \"/assets/app.js\", \"/assets/favicon.svg\")\n+    )\n+    created = client.post(\n+        \"/api/v1/forecasts\", json={\"symbol\": \"ACDC\", \"asset_type\": \"stock\"}\n+    ).json()\n+    prices = client.get(\n+        f\"/api/v1/history/{created['event']['id']}/prices\",\n+        params={\"series\": \"daily\", \"limit\": 10},\n+    )\n+\n+    assert asset_bytes < 96 * 1024\n+    assert prices.status_code == 200\n+    assert len(prices.content) < 8 * 1024\n",

              "file": "tools/browser/mcp-smoke.js",
              "patch": "Index: tools/browser/mcp-smoke.js\n===================================================================\n--- tools/browser/mcp-smoke.js\t\n+++ tools/browser/mcp-smoke.js\t\n@@ -0,0 +1,80 @@\n+// Exercise the configured MCP transport and a real headless Chromium context with bounded I/O.\n+const { spawn } = require(\"node:child_process\");\n+const fs = require(\"node:fs\");\n+const path = require(\"node:path\");\n+\n+const root = path.resolve(__dirname, \"../..\");\n+const config = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, \"opencode.json\"), \"utf8\"));\n+const [command, ...args] = config.mcp.playwright.command;\n+const child = spawn(command, args, { cwd: root, stdio: [\"pipe\", \"pipe\", \"pipe\"] });\n+let stdout = \"\";\n+let stderr = \"\";\n+let finished = false;\n+\n+function send(message) {\n+  child.stdin.write(`${JSON.stringify(message)}\\n`);\n+}\n+\n+function fail(message) {\n+  if (finished) return;\n+  finished = true;\n+  child.kill(\"SIGTERM\");\n+  console.error(`${message}${stderr ? `\\n${stderr}` : \"\"}`);\n+  process.exitCode = 1;\n+}\n+\n+const timer = setTimeout(() => fail(\"MCP smoke timed out after 20 seconds.\"), 20_000);\n+child.stderr.on(\"data\", (chunk) => {\n+  stderr += chunk.toString();\n+  if (stderr.length > 65_536) fail(\"MCP stderr exceeded its smoke-test limit.\");\n+});\n+child.stdout.on(\"data\", (chunk) => {\n+  stdout += chunk.toString();\n+  if (stdout.length > 1_048_576) return fail(\"MCP stdout exceeded its smoke-test limit.\");\n+  let newline;\n+  while ((newline = stdout.indexOf(\"\\n\")) >= 0) {\n+    const line = stdout.slice(0, newline).trim();\n+    stdout = stdout.slice(newline + 1);\n+    if (!line) continue;\n+    let message;\n+    try {\n+      message = JSON.parse(line);\n+    } catch (error) {\n+      return fail(`MCP returned invalid JSON: ${error.message}`);\n+    }\n+    if (message.id === 1) {\n+      send({ jsonrpc: \"2.0\", method: \"notifications/initialized\" });\n+      send({ jsonrpc: \"2.0\", id: 2, method: \"tools/list\", params: {} });\n+    } else if (message.id === 2) {\n+      const names = (message.result?.tools || []).map((tool) => tool.name);\n+      if (!names.includes(\"browser_tabs\")) return fail(\"Official browser tools were not listed.\");\n+      send({\n+        jsonrpc: \"2.0\",\n+        id: 3,\n+        method: \"tools/call\",\n+        params: { name: \"browser_tabs\", arguments: { action: \"list\" } },\n+      });\n+    } else if (message.id === 3) {\n+      if (message.error || message.result?.isError) return fail(\"Chromium context initialization failed.\");\n+      finished = true;\n+      clearTimeout(timer);\n+      child.kill(\"SIGTERM\");\n+      console.log(\"M06 MCP smoke passed: official tools and isolated Chromium responded.\");\n+    }\n+  }\n+});\n+child.on(\"error\", (error) => fail(`MCP process could not start: ${error.message}`));\n+child.on(\"exit\", (code) => {\n+  if (!finished) fail(`MCP process exited before completing the smoke test (${code}).`);\n+});\n+\n+send({\n+  jsonrpc: \"2.0\",\n+  id: 1,\n+  method: \"initialize\",\n+  params: {\n+    protocolVersion: \"2025-06-18\",\n+    capabilities: {},\n+    clientInfo: { name: \"stock-probs-m06-smoke\", version: \"1.0.0\" },\n+  },\n+});\n",
              "additions": 80,
              "deletions": 0,
              "status": "added"
            },

_trailing_missing_intraday_intervals(\n+    bars: tuple[Bar, ...], timezone: str, now: datetime\n+) -> int:\n+    \"\"\"Count eligible regular-session bars omitted after the latest completed response bar.\"\"\"\n+\n+    expected_end = _latest_scheduled_completed_end(now, timezone)\n+    if expected_end is None:\n+        return 0\n+    zone = ZoneInfo(timezone)\n+    completed_regular = []\n+    for bar in bars:\n+        local = bar.timestamp.astimezone(zone)\n+        close = scheduled_session_close(local.date(), timezone)\n+        session_open = datetime.combine(local.date(), time(9, 30), zone)\n+        if (\n+            close is not None\n+            and session_open <= local\n+            and bar.end <= close\n+            and bar.end.astimezone(UTC) <= now.astimezone(UTC)\n+ expected_end.astimezone(UTC):\n+        return 0\n+\n+    # Count only scheduled five-minute endpoints after the returned bar, never closed periods.\n+    missing = 0\n+    day = latest_end.astimezone(zone).date()\n+    expected_day = expected_end.astimezone(zone).date()\n+    while day <= expected_day:\n+        close = scheduled_session_close(day, timezone)\n+        if upper = min(close, expected_end) if day == expected_day else close\n+            if upper > lower:\n+                missing += int((upper - lower).total_seconds() // 300)\n+        day +=               "patch": "Index: tests/test_resource.py\n===================================================================\n--- tests/test_resource.py\t\n+++ tests/test_resource.py\t\n@@ -1,48 +1,54 @@\n \"\"\"M03/M06 resource smoke tests keep deterministic local work within explicit bounds.\"\"\"\n \n from __future__ import annotations\n \n import tracemalloc\n from datetime import UTC, datetime\n \n from stock_probs.provider import FixtureProvider\n from stock_probs.repository import Repository\n from stock_probs.service import ForecastService\n \n FIXED_NOW = datetime(2025, 1, 10, 17, 3, tzinfo=UTC)\n \n \n def test_bounded_fixture_forecast_batch_stays_small(settings):\n     repository = Repository(settings.database_path)\n     repository.migrate()\n     service = ForecastService(repository, FixtureProvider(), lambda: FIXED_NOW)\n \n     tracemalloc.start()\n     for index in range(20):\n         service.search(f\"LOAD{index}\", \"stock\")\n     _, peak = tracemalloc.get_traced_memory()\n     tracemalloc.stop()\n \n     # Twenty immutable snapshots cover a useful burst without desktop-scale memory or disk use.\n     assert peak < 64 * 1024 * 1024\n     assert settings.database_path.stat().st_size < 16 * 1024 * 1024\n     assert repository.history(page_size=100)[\"total\"] == 20\n \n \n def test_dashboard_and_price_slice_stay_lightweight(client):\n-    # The shell has no framework bundle, and chart consumers can request a tiny captured slice.\n+    # The shell/docs have no framework bundle, and chart consumers request a tiny captured slice.\n     asset_bytes = sum(\n         len(client.get(path).content)\n-        for path in (\"/\", \"/assets/app.css\", \"/assets/app.js\", \"/assets/favicon.svg\")\n+        for path in (\n+            \"/\",\n+            \"/api/v1/docs\",\n+            \"/assets/app.css\",\n+            \"/assets/app.js\",\n+            \"/assets/favicon.svg\",\n+        )\n     )\n     created = client.post(\n         \"/api/v1/forecasts\", json={\"symbol\": \"ACDC\", \"asset_type\": \"stock\"}\n     ).json()\n     prices = client.get(\n         f\"/api/v1/history/{created['event']['id']}/prices\",\n         params={\"series\": \"daily\", \"limit\": 10},\n     )\n \n     assert asset_bytes < 96 * 1024\n     assert prices.status_code == 200\n     assert len(prices.content) < 8 * 1024\n",

            "output": "<task id=\"ses_f72c4f276ffeJm9WRj0aBXCM1X\" state=\"completed\">\n<task_result>\n## Builder handoff\n\n**Tasks:** `R-M03-1`, `R-M03-2`, `R-M05-3`  \n**Status:** Implementation complete; independent QA/release gates remain pending.\n\n### Changes\n\n- `domain.py`\n  - Detects omitted scheduled daily sessions while excluding weekends and modeled holidays.\n  - Detects when the latest returned intraday bar precedes the latest eligible completed five-minute boundary.\n  - Marks affected forecasts `quality=stale`; no bars are fabricated.\n- `provider.py`\n  - Records omitted daily sessions and trailing completed intraday intervals.\n  - Eliminates `get_history_metadata()` calls.\n  - Reuses metadata cached by timeout-bounded history requests and fails closed if unavailable.\n- Added deterministic regressions in `test_domain.py` and `test_provider.py`.\n- Preserved holiday and early-close regressions.\n- No documentation, persistence, API, or presentation files edited.\n\n### Verification\n\nEnvironment: Linux ARM64, Python 3.11.2, commit baseline `cb7c1b179aa7b33c269e1e8ff41776328d7dccae`.\n\n- Repair and calendar regressions: **6 passed in 0.31s**\n- Focused domain/provider suite: **Pass**\n- Full non-live suite: **79 passed, 2 live tests deselected**\n- Coverage: **87.66%**, required 85%\n- Ruff across `src`, `tests`, and `scripts`: **Pass**\n- Compileall for changed files: **Pass**\n- Comment audit: **Pass — 45 implementation files**\n- `git diff --check`: **Pass**\n- Verification completed: `2026-09-10T21:38:20Z`\n\n### Limitations\n\n- Live Yahoo tests were intentionally deselected; no network claim is made.\n- Metadata extraction relies on the pinned yfinance 1.7 history-cache behavior.             "output": "<task id=\"ses_f72c4f1baffeECZSQ37ujzSmCJ\" state=\"completed\">\n<task_result>\nImplemented repair lane C without commits, pushes, or documentation/API/static/provider changes.\n\n### Changes\n\n- Added per-installation 256-bit local trust key and HMAC-SHA256 manifest authentication.\n  - Key stored outside the backup directory.\n  - Key and artifacts hardened to `0600`.\n  - Missing/invalid keys are never regenerated during restore.\n  - Unsigned, forged, or checksum/count-recomputed manifests fail before database extraction.\n- Added bounded ZIP preflight:\n  - Exactly two entries required.\n  - Central-directory metadata capped at 16 KiB.\n  - Unsafe flags, compression, symlink metadata, offsets, and sizes rejected.\n- Hardened runtime storage:\n  - Data/backup directories: `0700`.\n  - SQLite database/sidecars, trust key, and artifacts: `0600`.\n  - Descriptor-based `O_NOFOLLOW` checks prevent chmod following final symlinks.\n- Added regressions covering forgery, unsigned manifests, entry floods, oversized metadata, key loss, permissive paths/files, symlinks, round-trip restore, and non-destructive failures.\n\n### Verification — 2026-09-10T21:43:05Z\n\n- Focused tests: **35 passed**\n- Full non-live suite: **79 passed, 2 deselected**, coverage **89.02%**\n- `make restore-test`: **26 passed**\n- Scoped Ruff lint: **Pass**\n- Scoped Ruff security rules: **Pass**\n- Mypy backup/CLI boundary: **Pass**\n- Comment audit: **Pass — 45 files**\n- Operational CLI migrate → backup → verify → promote plus permission assertions: **Pass**\n\n### Limitation\n\nThe final aggregate `make check` rerun was blocked by concurrent, out-of-scope changes in `src/stock_probs/api.py`: unused `pydantic.Field` and an overlong line. The performance of two models in the FHS family with different devolatilising methods is illustrated. Clark\n-Highlights:\n-Filtered historical simulation with an underlying GARCH process can be used as a valuable tool in VaR analysis, as it derives risk estimates that are sensitive to the distributional properties of the historical data of the produced predictive density. I examine the applications to risk analysis that filtered historical simulation can provide, as well as an interpretation of the predictive density as a poor man’s Bayesian posterior distribution. The predictive density allows us to make associated probabilistic statements regarding the results for VaR analysis, giving greater measurement of risk and the ability to maintain the optimal level of risk per tolerance in portfolios to remain compliant with regulations. Keywords: Filtered Historical Simulation, Predictive Density, Value at Risk, VaR, GARCH\n-...\n-Filtered historical simulation was first introduced by Barone-Adesi, Giannopoulos and Vosper (1999). It is a great method for determining VaR for portfolios, as it uses both nonlinear econo metric models and historical returns to build the predictive density that the portfolio could take for multiple days looking forward. Rather than most models, which suffer the problem of under estimating the risk of extreme outcomes, filtered historical simulation risk estimated are derived directly from the tails of the distribution. In filtered historical simulation, price series are not forced to conform to a probability distribu tion, but the data are allowed to speak for themselves. Historical data is still considered. This is an important aspect to filtered historical simulation since a basic Monte Carlo simulation only draws from a theoretical distribution, which smooths the empirical distribution and may underestimate the risk of catastrophe. It generates thousands of scenarios for the mean and variance of each risk factor in a multi-period horizon. This allows filtered historical simulation to provide a more accurate depiction of the tail structure in future prices. These features make filtered historical simulation very easy to implement in risk analysis and stress-testing. Filtered historical simulation works by using a parametric model of return volatility, such as a GARCH model, to simulate log returns over some predefined risk horizon. Using the estimated GARCH model\n-...\n-, filtered historical simulation will assume that GARCH draws from the standardized empirical distribution, so therefore the standardized innovations are et = rt/σˆt. rt represents the historical daily log return and σˆ2 t represents the GARCH daily standard deviation. The simulation process begins by setting initial conditions σ˜0 and r˜0. r˜0 will be set equal to the log return from the previous day, but there are at least two different options for setting σ˜0. The first of the two options is setting σ˜0 equal to the last estimated daily conditional volatility from the GARCH model. The second option is to set σ˜0 equal to the long run unconditional volatility:\n-...\n-To calculate the VaR through filtered historical simulation, first I need to estimate a GARCH model to account for volatility clustering patterns as seen above. I used the optimizer ‘rugarch’ from R to optimize the GARCH parameters ωˆ , αˆ, and βˆ. These are the estimated parameters that were used in the i.i.d. bootstrap process for filtered historical simulation. The full S&P 500 and IBM code can be found in the linked Github Repository (Clark, Tyson (2019)). As is shown by Mc Donald (2009), there are jumps in the return data for IBM surrounding earnings announcements that the GARCH model has difficulty explaining, so those 5 particular dates have been omitted from the optimization process. After the optimizer has found the values of ωˆ , αˆ, and βˆ, they can be used in the i.i.d. bootstrap process of filtered historical simulation. I will first find the scaled volatility adjusted VaR using the GARCH process to compare my results in filtered historical simulation.\n-...\n-As is shown in this table, the adjusted GARCH model overestimates risk when compared to filtered historical simulation. This is because the square root scaling of a daily VaR model estimated through GARCH doesn’t allow for mean reversion, and will subsequently overestimate the VaR when taken on a day with a higher than usual variance. This is why it is important to use the statistical bootstrap, and why filtered historical simulation is better than a simple square root adjustment to a single day GARCH estimation. This will hold in almost all of the 10,000 simulations carried out. We can see this distribution in the produced predictive density. My simulated predictive density is shown below.\n-...\n-This produced predictive density helps us see the distribution of returns through a bootstrap of 10,000 simulations. This distribution can be quite useful when a bank or investment manager is looking at the VaR for his or her respective portfolio. The density is computed using frequentist methods, but can be looked at as a poor-man’s Bayesian posterior distribution when there is an uninformed prior, as is most likely the case with a VaR model (Murphy (2012)). In fact, the way filtered historical simulation is modeled, it is very similar to a Bayesian model. Without getting too involved in the Bayesian perspective, Bayes’ rule can be defined as:\n-...\n-, where P(θ) is the prior applied to the Bayesian model. It can be seen that when this prior is uninformed, it will drop out, leaving just P(x| θ), which will be informed by the model just as filtered historical simulation. It is shown here that the actual VaR model is being computed using frequentist methods, but this produced density is the frequentist approach to a Bayesian posterior. I would like to quote Terry Speed about how ‘We don’t need to be Bayesian; we just need to be approximately so. We don’t need theory to tell us our method works; we just need to simulate and see’ (Speed (2011)). This Bayesian interpretation can be important. In ‘Computer Age Statistical Inference’, Efron and Hastie provide some comparisons between frequentist methods and Bayesian methods (Efron and Hastie (2016)). An important note they make is that a Bayesian places a large bet on his or her prior being correct, or at least not harmful, but a frequentist will take a more defensive approach, that by statistical methods he or she can produce a useful distribution, regardless of the true µ. In the perspective of filtered historical simulation for VaR, this is an important point since there can be no prior belief regarding the distribution of returns if one wants to properly account for risk, especially in the tails. Though calculated using frequentist method, the distribution shown above is very close to a Bayesian posterior distribution. When a risk manager or trader is thinking about risk, they can’t think about these frequentist models. Though the models may do a good job of summarizing data, the true uncertainty must be thought of from a subjective sense. Filtered historical simulation produces a predictive density that allows traders and risk managers to do just that. Though filtered historical simulation is a fre quentist method, rarely, if ever, is the produced distribution thought of from a Bayesian subjective sense, though that is exactly what the model is producing. This way of thinking about uncertainty incorporates the theory that prices reflect information, or tacit knowledge, rather than just being something that is calculated through a model (Hayek (1945)). This way of thinking will help risk managers and traders more properly account for risk in their models, and is a great way to look at filtered historical simulation.\n-...\n-(Barone-Adesi, Giannopoulos and Vosper (1999)). In contrast to some other techniques where the scenarios are generated ad hoc, FHS uses a combination of nonlinear econometric models and past returns to build the probability distribution of possible values that the asset (risk factor) could take in the days ahead. Risk estimates are directly derived from the tails of the distribution. \n-\n-The FHS is a kind of historical simulation since uses past returns as innovations in modeling the randomness of the asset prices. It has however one major improvement; the row returns are first scaled by the volatility that prevailed that day and then are multiplied by the current forecast of volatility. The first pass, the scaling, is necessary in order to make the past returns stationary and to render them suitable innovations for a simulation process. The second step, the re-scaling, endows the historical returns to reflect the current volatility conditions prevailing in the markets.\n-...\n-From the statistical perspective the FHS is seen as a semi-parametric model. The price series is not forced to conform to any kind of probability distribution, but rather the data are allowed to talk themselves. Risk estimation is highly dependent on good prediction of uncommon events, or catastrophic risk. Simulation models that draw innovations from theoretical distributions, such as the parametric Monte Carlo, indeed smooth the empirical distribution of the data and consequently they may underestimate \"catastrophic risk\" \n-\n-The cross dependencies among the series are handled through parallel bootstrapping. This reduces dramatically the dimensions of the problem because the number of parameters and the time needed to carry out the computation increases linearly with the number of securities or risk factors in the portfolio. In contrast, in models that are relying on the variance-covariance matrix to capture the cross dependencies, the dimension is a quadratic function of the number of securities that are handled.\n-...\n-In summary, the FHS combines\n-...\n-best features from other risk management models. \n-\n-- The data do not have to follow a unique or a pre-specified distribution (it uses the historical or empirical distribution). Thus it allows for fat tails, volatility clusters and changing means.\n-- It goes around the bias problem of using just historical data.\n-- It handles easily dependencies across very large numbers of assets.\n-...\n-- Generates thousands of scenarios for the mean and variance of each risk factor in a multi-period horizon. This provides a more accurate formation of the structure in the tails of possible price realizations. \n-- Non linear instruments such options are re-priced each day ahead in the risk horizon. The re-pricing handles the risk with unbalanced portfolios found in the expiring contracts before the end of the investment horizon.\n-...\n-- Stress testing, sensitivity analysis and coherent risk measures are easily implemented.\n-\n----\n-\n-Title: Predictive Distributions via Filtered Historical Simulation for ...\n-URL: https://digitalcommons.usu.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2394&context=gradreports\n-Published: N/A\n-Author: Tyson Clark\n-Highlights:\n-Filtered historical simulation with an underlying GARCH process can be used as a valuable tool in VaR analysis, as it derives risk estimates that are sensitive to the distributional properties of the historical data of the produced predictive density. Filtered\n-\n----\n-\n-Title: Value-at-Risk Forecasting Ability of Filtered Historical Simulation for Non-Normal GARCH Returns\n-URL: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2133238\n-Published: N/A\n-Author: N/A\n-Highlights:\n-As a hybrid methodology to estimate VaR, that combines the use of parametric modelling with the use of bootstrapping techniques, filtered historical simulation (FHS) should not be sensitive to the use of alternative distributions assumed in the filtering stage. However, recent studies (Kuester et al. 2006) have found that the distribution used in the filtering stage can influence the VaR estimates obtained in the context of this methodology. Using Extreme Value Theory (EVT) this paper explains that the VaR estimates for lower probabilities should not be sensitive to the distribution assumed in the filtering stage of the FHS method. However, for higher probabilities, the EVT results do not hold and therefore the use of alternative distributions might impact the VaR estimates. These theoretical results are tested using both simulated and real data. Three different realistic data generating processes were considered to generate several series of simulated returns. Additionally, three competing models, differing in the innovations assumption, were tested: a normal-GARCH, a t-GARCH and a skew-t-GARCH. Our backtesting results indicate that FHS can forecast VaR with accuracy for data which exhibits a high incidence of zeros, time-varying skewness, asymmetric effects to return shocks on volatility, as well as other stylized facts. Importantly, our results for the simulated data demonstrate that, for lower probabilities, the choice of the distribution assumed in the filtering stage has no impact on the performance of FHS as an accurate method to forecasting VaR. Additionally, 40 years of daily data on six well known active stock indices are used to empirically evaluate the FHS VaR estimates. Four competing GARCH-type specifications, combined with three different innovation assumptions (normal, Student-t and skew-Student t), are used to capture time series dynamics. Based on a sample of several VaR probabilities, the results of the dynamic quantile (DQ) tests clearly indicate that the use of asymmetric GARCH models (specifically GJR and GJR in Mean) generally improve the VaR forecasting performance of FHS. In addition, the choice of a skew-Student t distribution for the innovation process slightly improves the performance results of the GJR in Mean model. When different VaR probabilities are used, the choice of an appropriate model specification seems to be more important than the choice of a suitable distribution assumption. Relinquish the shared lock on the database file obtained in step 1. \n-\n- This\n-...\n-## 2.2. Possible Enhancements\n-\n- The implementation of this function could be enhanced in at least two ways: \n-\n-1. Failing to obtain the lock on database file zFilename (an SQLITE_BUSY error) could be handled, and \n-2. Cases where the page-sizes of database pInMemory and zFilename are different could be handled better. \n-\n- Since database zFilename is a file on disk, then it may be accessed externally by another process. This means that when the call to sqlite3_backup_step() attempts to read from or write data to it, it may fail to obtain the required file lock. If this happens, this implementation will fail, returning SQLITE_BUSY immediately. The solution would be to register a busy-handler callback or timeout with database connection pFile using sqlite3_busy_handler() or sqlite3_busy_timeout() as soon as it is opened. If it fails to obtain a required lock immediately, sqlite3_backup_step() uses any registered busy-handler callback or timeout in the same way as sqlite3_step() or sqlite3_exec() does. \n-\n- Usually, it does not matter if the page-sizes of the source database and the destination database are different before the contents of the destination are overwritten. The page-size of the destination database is simply changed as part of the backup operation. The exception is if the destination database happens to be an in-memory database. In this case, if the page sizes are not the same at the start of the backup operation, then the operation fails with an SQLITE_READONLY error. Unfortunately, this could occur when loading a database image from a file into an in-memory database using function loadOrSaveDb(). \n-\n- However, if in-memory database pInMemory has just been opened (and is therefore completely empty) before being passed to function loadOrSaveDb(), then it is still possible to change its page size using an SQLite \"PRAGMA page_size\" command. Function loadOrSaveDb() could detect this case, and attempt to set the page-size of the in-memory database to the page-size of database zFilename before invoking the online backup API functions. \n-\n-# 3. Example 2: Online Backup of a Running Database\n-...\n-int backupDb(\n-  sqlite3 *pDb,               /* Database to back up */\n-  const char *zFilename,      /* Name of file to back up to */\n-  void(*xProgress)(int, int)  /* Progress function to invoke */     \n-){\n-  int rc;                     /* Function return code */\n-  sqlite3 *pFile;             /* Database connection opened on zFilename */\n-  sqlite3_backup *pBackup;    /* Backup handle used to copy data */\n-\n-  /* Open the database file identified by zFilename. */\n-  rc = sqlite3_open(zFilename, &pFile);\n-  if( rc==SQLITE_OK ){\n-\n-    /* Open the sqlite3_backup object used to accomplish the transfer */\n-    pBackup = sqlite3_backup_init(pFile, \"main\", pDb, \"main\");\n-    if( pBackup ){\n-\n-      /* Each iteration of this loop copies 5 database pages from database\n-      ** pDb to the backup database. If the return value of backup_step()\n-      ** indicates that there are still further pages to copy, sleep for\n-      ** 250 ms before repeating. */\n-      do {\n-        rc = sqlite3_backup_step(pBackup, 5);\n-        xProgress(\n-            sqlite3_backup_remaining(pBackup),\n-            sqlite3_backup_pagecount(pBackup)\n-        );\n-        if( rc==SQLITE_OK || rc==SQLITE_BUSY || rc==SQLITE_LOCKED ){\n-          sqlite3_sleep(250);\n-        }\n-      } while( rc==SQLITE_OK || rc==SQLITE_BUSY || rc==SQLITE_LOCKED );\n-\n-      /* Release resources allocated by backup_init(). */\n-      (void)sqlite3_backup_finish(pBackup);\n-    }\n-    rc = sqlite3_errcode(pFile);\n-  }\n-  \n-  /* Close the database connection opened on database file zFilename\n-  ** and return the result of this function. */\n-  (void)sqlite3_close(pFile);\n-  return rc;\n-}\n-...\n-```\n-\n- The function presented in the previous example copies the entire source database in one call to sqlite3_backup_step(). This requires holding a read-lock on the source database file for the duration of the operation, preventing any other database user from writing to the database. It also holds the mutex associated with database pInMemory throughout the copy, preventing any other thread from using it. The C function in this section, designed to be called by a background thread or process for creating a backup of an online database, avoids these problems using the following approach: \n-\n-1. Function sqlite3_backup_init() is called to create an sqlite3_backup object to copy data from database pDb to the backup database file identified by zFilename. \n-2. Function sqlite3_backup_step() is called with a parameter of 5 to copy 5 pages of database pDb to the backup database (file zFilename). \n-3. If there are still more pages to copy from database pDb, then the function sleeps for 250 milliseconds (using the sqlite3_sleep() utility) and then returns to step 2. \n-4. Function sqlite3_backup_finish() is called to clean up resources allocated by sqlite3_backup_init().\n-...\n-## 3.1. File and Database Connection Locking\n-\n- During the 250 ms sleep in step 3 above, no read-lock is held on the database file and the mutex associated with pDb is not held. This allows other threads to use database connection pDb and other connections to write to the underlying database file. \n-\n- If another thread or process writes to the source database while this function is sleeping, then SQLite detects this and usually restarts the backup process when sqlite3_backup_step() is next called. There is one exception to this rule: If the source database is not an in-memory database, and the write is performed from within the same process as the backup operation and uses the same database handle (pDb), then the destination database (the one opened using connection pFile) is automatically updated along with the source. The backup process may then be continued after the sqlite3_sleep() call returns as if nothing had happened. \n-\n- Whether or not the backup process is restarted as a result of writes to the source database mid-backup, the user can be sure that when the backup operation is completed the backup database contains a consistent and up-to-date snapshot of the original. However: \n-\n-- Writes to an in-memory source database, or writes to a file-based source database by an external process or thread using a database connection other than pDb are significantly more expensive than writes made to a file-based source database using pDb (as the entire backup operation must be restarted in the former two cases). \n-- If the backup process is restarted frequently enough it may never run to completion and the backupDb() function may never return. \n-\n-## 3.2. backup_remaining() and backup_pagecount()\n-\n- The backupDb() function uses the sqlite3_backup_remaining() and sqlite3_backup_pagecount() functions to report its progress via the user-supplied xProgress() callback. Function sqlite3_backup_remaining() returns the number of pages left to copy and sqlite3_backup_pagecount() returns the total number of pages in the source database (in this case the database opened by pDb). So the percentage completion of the process may be calculated as: \n-\n- Completion = 100% * (pagecount() - remaining()) / pagecount() \n-\n- The sqlite3_backup_remaining() and sqlite3_backup_pagecount() APIs report values stored by the previous call to sqlite3_backup_step(), they do not actually inspect the source database file. This means that if the source database is written to by another thread or process after the call to sqlite3_backup_step() returns but before the values returned by sqlite3_backup_remaining() and sqlite3_backup_pagecount() are used, the values may be technically incorrect. This is not usually a problem. \n-\n-This page was last updated on 2025-11-13 07:12:58Z\n-\n----\n-\n-Title: Online Backup API.\n-URL: https://sqlite.org/c3ref/backup_finish.html\n-Published: N/A\n-Author: N/A\n-Highlights:\n-> ```\n-> sqlite3_backup *sqlite3_backup_init(\n-> sqlite3 *pDest, /* Destination database handle */\n-> const char *zDestName, /* Destination database name */\n-> sqlite3 *pSource, /* Source database handle */\n-> const char *zSourceName /* Source database name */\n-> );\n-> int sqlite3_backup_step(sqlite3_backup *p, int nPage);\n-> int sqlite3_backup_finish(sqlite3_backup *p);\n-> int sqlite3_backup_remaining(sqlite3_backup *p);\n-> int sqlite3_backup_pagecount(sqlite3_backup *p);\n-> \n-> ```\n-\n- The backup API copies the content of one database into another. It is useful either for creating backups of databases or for copying in-memory databases to or from persistent files.\n-...\n-SQLite holds a write transaction open on the destination database file for the duration of the backup operation. The source database is read-locked only while it is being read; it is not locked continuously for the entire backup operation. Thus, the backup may be performed on a live source database without preventing other database connections from reading or writing to the source database while the backup is underway.\n-...\n-To perform a backup operation: \n-\n-1. sqlite3_backup_init() is called once to initialize the backup, \n-2. sqlite3_backup_step() is called one or more times to transfer the data between the two databases, and finally \n-3. sqlite3_backup_finish() is called to release all resources associated with the backup operation. \n-\n- There should be exactly one call to sqlite3_backup_finish() for each successful call to sqlite3_backup_init().\n-\n- sqlite3_backup_init()\n-...\n-Function sqlite3_backup_step(B,N) will copy up to N pages between the source and destination databases specified by sqlite3_backup object B. If sqlite3_backup_step(B,N) successfully finishes copying all pages from source to destination, then it returns SQLITE_DONE. If an error occurs while running sqlite3_backup_step(B,N), then an error code is returned. As well as SQLITE_OK and SQLITE_DONE, a call to sqlite3_backup_step() may return SQLITE_READONLY, SQLITE_NOMEM, SQLITE_BUSY, SQLITE_LOCKED, or an SQLITE_IOERR_XXX extended error code.\n-...\n-The sqlite3_backup_step() might return SQLITE_READONLY if \n-\n-1. the destination database was opened read-only, or \n-2. the destination database is using write-ahead-log journaling and the destination and source page sizes differ, or \n-3. the destination database is an in-memory database and the destination and source page sizes differ. \n-\n-If sqlite3_backup_step() cannot obtain a required file-system lock, then the busy-handler function is invoked (if one is specified). If the busy-handler returns non-zero before the lock is available, then SQLITE_BUSY is returned to the caller. In this case the call to sqlite3_backup_step() can be retried later. If the source database connection is being used to write to the source database when sqlite3_backup_step() is called, then SQLITE_LOCKED is returned immediately. Again, in this case the call to sqlite3_backup_step() can be retried later on. If SQLITE_IOERR_XXX, SQLITE_NOMEM, or SQLITE_READONLY is returned, then there is no point in retrying the call to sqlite3_backup_step(). These errors are considered fatal.
