What the application will show\n-\n-### Analysis dashboard\n-\n-A compact dashboard with:\n-\n-- **Company/ticker search**, displaying company name, exchange, and currency before selection.\n-- Forecast mode and historical “as of” controls.\n-- Reference price, reference timestamp, target close, and data freshness.\n-- Probability of **up, down, and unchanged**.\n-- Estimated median move and **50%, 80%, and 95% prediction intervals**.\n-- Typical gain conditional on rising, and typical loss conditional on falling.\n-- Probabilities for configurable thresholds, initially **±1%, ±3%, ±5%, and ±10%**.\n-- Historical price chart and predicted return-distribution chart.\n-- Sample size, model version, and available out-of-sample performance.\n-\n-The probabilities describe the price **at the target close**. A probability of closing down 5% is a different calculation from touching a 5% decline during the day; the interface will name the event precisely.\n-\n-### History and comparison\n-\n-A searchable history page will support:\n-- Symbol, company name, original search text, date range, mode, and success/failure filters.\n-- Reopening the **original saved result**.\n-- Running a fresh analysis from an old query.\n-- Comparing saved predictions with realized returns.\n-- CSV and JSON export.\n-\n-### Visual design\n-\n-Use a responsive layout with clear typography, restrained color, accessible contrast, and optional dark mode. Charts will have readable numerical summaries, keyboard-accessible controls, and explicit loading, stale-data, and empty states.\n-\n-Charts will be downsampled for display, while calculations use the complete eligible data. Chart.js documents downsampling and reduced animation as effective performance measures.[1]\n-\n----\n-\n-## 3. Forecasting approach\n-\n-### A. Close-to-close: deliver first\n-\n-**Definition:** use data through the latest completed trading session to estimate the return to the next trading session’s close.\n-\n-Recommended initial model: **volatility-adjusted historical simulation**.\n-\n-1. Retrieve up to ten years of available daily history.\n-2. Establish a consistent, split-adjusted **price-return** series, retaining dividends and other corporate actions separately.\n-3. Calculate historical returns and volatility using only information available at each historical cutoff.\n-4. Standardize historical shocks by their contemporaneous volatility.\n-5. Rescale those shocks to the current volatility estimate.\n-6. Derive direction probabilities, thresholds, conditional moves, and prediction intervals from that single distribution.\n-\n-This is a small numerical calculation suitable for the laptop. It retains historical asymmetry and large moves while responding to changes in volatility. Filtered historical simulation is an established technique, although its performance depends on the volatility estimate and available sample.[2]\n-\n-**Important modeling expectation:** volatility adjustment primarily improves estimates of move size and tail risk. Directional probabilities may remain close to historical frequencies. Any additional trend/volume-based directional model should earn its place through out-of-sample evaluation.\n-\n-The original subjective weighting and mock “best weights” calculation will be replaced by this data-derived approach.\n-\n-### B. Intraday: a separately evaluated model\n-\n-**Definition:** estimate the move from the newest eligible intraday observation to the upcoming regular-session close.\n-\n-Recommended first implementation:\n-- Use the latest available **completed five-minute bar** as the reproducible forecast reference.\n-- Display its timestamp and age prominently; a newer quote can appear separately.\n-- Construct historical returns from comparable intraday cutoffs to their session closes.\n-- Compare observations at equivalent exchange-local times/session types.\n-- Evaluate intraday forecasts separately from daily forecasts.\n-\n-During an open session, the target is that session’s close. Closed-market requests will clearly identify the next target session and the available regular-session reference price.\n-\n-**Research constraint:** yfinance’s implementation limits five-minute history to approximately **60 calendar days**. That is a small number of independent trading sessions, especially for estimating rare 5–10% moves.[3]\n-\n-Therefore:\n-- Archive retrieved intraday bars locally.\n-- Backfill available gaps when the application resumes.\n-- Display limited-sample status where appropriate.\n-- Return an explicit insufficient-data result when a calculation is unsupported.\n-- Treat observations from the same session as dependent during evaluation.\n-\n-### C. Honest historical replay\n-\n-There will be two distinct historical views:\n-\n-| View | Meaning |\n-|---|---|\n-| Saved forecast | The actual inputs and result recorded by this application at the time |\n-| Historical reconstruction | A calculation made now using historical observations cut off at the selected date |\n-\n-Yahoo can revise historical prices and adjustments. A reconstruction made today cannot establish exactly what Yahoo served yesterday unless that earlier data was saved.\n-\n-Current news, financial statements, and earnings information can be displayed as timestamped context. Incorporating them into a historical model requires reliable publication-time data; retrospective current metadata must not enter past forecasts.\n-\n-### D. Verification of the model\n-\n-Use chronological, walk-forward evaluation:\n-- Train using earlier observations.\n-- Predict subsequent observations.\n-- Keep a final evaluation period separate from model selection.\n-- Compare against simple historical-frequency and distribution baselines.\n-- Measure direction/threshold **Brier scores**, reliability plots, and prediction-interval coverage.\n-- Report performance by symbol, mode, sample size, and evaluation period.\n-\n-Time-ordered validation avoids training on future observations.[4] Brier scores measure overall probability quality; reliability plots are also needed to assess calibration.[5]\n-\n-A rare event that has never appeared in the sample will be presented as **“no observations among N cases,”** with uncertainty, rather than as an impossible event.\n-\n----\n-\n-## 4. Simple application architecture\n-\n-```text\n-Browser\n-  └─ FastAPI application\n-       ├─ HTML pages + small JavaScript modules + Chart.js\n-       ├─ Search / forecast / history routes\n-       ├─ Yahoo Finance adapter\n-       ├─ Forecast and evaluation functions\n-       └─ SQLite storage and backup utilities\n-```\n-\n-| Layer | Choice |\n-|---|---|\n-| Backend | Python, FastAPI, one Uvicorn worker |\n-| Frontend | Jinja2 templates, CSS, small JavaScript modules |\n-| Charts | Locally served, pinned Chart.js |\n-| Market data | yfinance behind one application-owned adapter |\n-| Numerical work | NumPy/pandas; SciPy where needed |\n-| Trading sessions | `exchange_calendars` |\n-| Persistence | Python’s built-in `sqlite3` |\n-| Dependency management | `pyproject.toml` and a committed `uv.lock` |\n-| Checks | pytest, Ruff, mypy, targeted browser tests |\n-\n-Blocking Yahoo requests will run outside the async event loop with bounded concurrency. FastAPI explicitly supports this pattern for synchronous libraries.[6]\n-\n-### Proposed project boundaries\n-\n-```text\n-src/stock_probs/\n-  app.py                 # Web application\n-  cli.py                 # Serve, migrate, backup, restore, evaluate\n-  providers/yahoo.py     # Yahoo-specific behavior\n-  forecasting/           # Daily/intraday models and evaluation\n-  services.py            # Fetch → validate → forecast → save\n-  db.py                  # Connections and parameterized queries\n-  templates/\n-  static/\n-migrations/\n-tests/\n-docs/\n-```\n-\n-Long design material belongs in `docs/PLAN.md` and `docs/MODEL.md`. The requested root `AGENTS.md` will remain compact, containing verified commands and repository-specific pitfalls.\n-\n-### Freshness and performance\n-\n-- Fetch symbols on demand.\n-- Refresh daily data when a new session may have completed.\n-- Use bounded intraday refreshes and pause browser polling when hidden.\n-- Coalesce simultaneous requests for the same data.\n-- Apply timeouts, limited retries, and backoff for Yahoo failures.\n-- Preserve usable cached results with their original timestamps.\n-- Load calendars and market data only for requested instruments.\n-\n-Proposed acceptance targets, to be measured on this laptop:\n-- Normal server memory below **500 MiB**.\n-- Cached single-symbol analysis below **1 second**.\n-- Indexed history searches below **250 ms** on a 100,000-query fixture.\n-- No continuous background CPU consumption while idle.\n-\n-Network-dependent latency will be measured separately.\n-\n----\n-\n-## 5. SQLite, searchable history, and backups\n-\n-### Core records\n-\n-| Record | Stored information |\n-|---|---|\n-| Instruments | Canonical symbol, company, exchange, currency, timezone |\n-| Market bars | Daily/intraday OHLCV, corporate actions, timestamps, provenance |\n-| Queries | Original input, parameters, time, status, error details |\n-| Input snapshots | Immutable, compressed, deduplicated inputs used by forecasts |\n-| Forecasts | Probabilities, intervals, reference/target times, model/configuration version |\n-| Outcomes | Observed return and scoring results linked to the original forecast |\n-\n-Every submitted company/symbol search, analysis, historical replay, and refresh will be recorded—including failures and repeated requests. Browser autocomplete keystrokes will be treated as interface activity rather than submitted queries.\n-\n-Queries will be recorded before provider work begins. Interrupted work can then be identified after a restart.\n-\n-Use indexed filters plus SQLite full-text search for original query text and company names. Historical results will remain readable offline.\n-\n-### Database behavior\n-\n-Use:\n-- Explicit transactions and foreign keys.\n-- Short writes, with network calls outside transactions.\n-- Connections owned by the thread performing the operation.\n-- A busy timeout.\n-- Versioned SQL migrations.\n-\n-**For this installation, start with rollback-journal mode.** SQLite documents a WAL-reset corruption issue affecting versions including the installed 3.40.1 under particular concurrent conditions. Rollback journaling is suitable for this workload; WAL can be reconsidered with a verified patched SQLite runtime.[7]\n-\n-### Backups\n-\n-Implement:\n-- Automatic backup when due while the application is running.\n-- A backup before schema migrations.\n-- A manual backup command.\n-- SQLite’s online backup API.\n-- Integrity checks before a backup is marked successful.\n-- Configurable retention and disk-space checks.\n-- A restore command that operates while the application is stopped.\n-- A tested restore into a separate database.\n-\n-Python’s SQLite backup API supports consistent backups while the source database is being accessed.[8]\n-\n-The backup destination can be an external drive. **Git revisions preserve application code; database backups preserve searches, market data, and forecasts.** Query history will have no automatic expiry.\n-\n----\n-\n-## 6. Secure implementation requirements\n-\n-For the confirmed laptop-only deployment:\n-\n-- Bind the server to `127.0.0.1`.\n-- Validate allowed Host and Origin headers and protect state-changing requests against CSRF.\n-- Use parameterized SQL and allowlisted sort/filter fields.\n-- Validate lengths, date ranges, thresholds, and Yahoo-compatible symbols.\n-- Accept stock identifiers rather than user-supplied fetch URLs.\n-- Escape company names, query text, and provider messages in HTML.\n-- Serve scripts locally under a restrictive Content Security Policy.\n-- Keep databases, backups, secrets, logs, and Yahoo cookie caches outside public static paths.\n-- Use restrictive permissions for application data.\n-- Pin dependencies and run vulnerability checks.\n-- Restrict restore operations to the local CLI.\n-- Sanitize spreadsheet exports against formula injection.\n-\n-Origin verification and CSRF defenses remain relevant to local browser applications.[9]\n-\n----\n-\n-## 7. Actionable implementation and Git gates\n-\n-Each milestone follows **implement → verify → review diff → commit → push → verify remote state**.\n-\n-| Gate | Actionable deliverables | Required verification |\n-|---|---|---|\n-| **1. Foundation** | Add `AGENTS.md`, README, design documents, package structure, lockfile, `.gitignore`; archive prototypes; untrack virtual environments while preserving local installations; establish GitHub access | Reproducible ARM installation; clean imports; review tracked files and credentials |\n-| **2. Persistence** | Implement migrations, query records, immutable snapshots, history repository, backup/restore CLI | Restart persistence, failed/interrupted query recording, snapshot immutability, backup/restore round trip |\n-| **3. Yahoo integration** | Add symbol/company search, daily retrieval, metadata, exchange calendars, cache policy, error handling | Fixtures for missing data, rate limits, splits, currency units, holidays, early closes, and incomplete bars; small live smoke check |\n-| **4. Daily forecasting** | Implement baseline and volatility-adjusted distributions, thresholds, historical reconstruction, outcome scoring, walk-forward reports | Future-data exclusion, probability consistency, ordered intervals, reference-price consistency, documented evaluation |\n-| **5. Dashboard — v0.1** | Build search, analysis cards, charts, query history, original-result views, exports, backup status | Browser journey from search to saved forecast to restart and retrieval; accessibility and ARM performance checks |\n-| **6. Intraday forecasts** | Add five-minute acquisition/archive, matched-cutoff model, freshness handling, session-specific targets | Cutoff alignment, partial-bar exclusion, session-grouped evaluation, limited-sample behavior, closed-market handling |\n-| **7. Full release — v0.2** | Complete security checks, documentation, CI, resource measurements, and startup workflow; update `AGENTS.md` with verified commands | Both modes exercised end-to-end; restore drill; clean installation; source and release tag verified on GitHub |\n-\n-### Essential correctness tests\n-\n-The highest-value tests are:\n-\n-1. Appending future prices cannot change an earlier forecast.\n-2. Updating Yahoo’s cached history cannot change a saved forecast.\n-3. Downside probabilities decrease as the loss threshold increases.\n-4. Up, down, and unchanged probabilities sum to one.\n-5. Prediction intervals are correctly ordered and use the displayed reference price.\n-6. Splits and currency changes do not become artificial crashes.\n-7. Incomplete daily/intraday bars cannot enter completed-period inputs.\n-8. Search and forecast history survives restart and backup restoration.\n-9. Provider failures are recorded and distinguishable from successful forecasts.\n-10. Input and export handling resist SQL injection, XSS, and spreadsheet formula injection.\n-\n-Live Yahoo tests will be opt-in. Deterministic tests will use controlled fixtures.\n-\n-### Proposed developer commands\n-\n-These are commands to implement during scaffolding; they do not exist yet:\n-\n-```bash\n-uv sync --locked\n-\n-uv run stock-probs db migrate\n-uv run stock-probs serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000\n-\n-uv run ruff format --check src tests\n-uv run ruff check src tests\n-uv run mypy src/stock_probs\n-uv run pytest -q -m \"not live and not browser\"\n-\n-uv run pytest tests/test_daily_forecast.py -q\n-uv run stock-probs backup\n-uv run stock-probs restore --from /path/to/backup.sqlite3\n-```\n-\n-The foundation gate will install/authenticate `gh` as needed and verify the existing repository. Releases will carry explicit application/model versions and Git tags.\n-\n----\n-\n-## Research references\n-\n-1. Playwright supports all modern rendering engines including Chromium, WebKit, and Firefox. Test on Windows, Linux, and macOS, locally or on CI, headless or headed with native mobile emulation.\n-\n-The [Playwright library](/python/docs/library) can be used as a general purpose browser automation tool, providing a powerful set of APIs to automate web applications, for both sync and async Python.\n-\n-This introduction describes the Playwright Pytest plugin, which is the recommended way to write end-to-end tests.\n-\n-**You will learn**\n-\n--   [How to install Playwright Pytest](/python/docs/intro#installing-playwright-pytest)\n--   [How to run the example test](/python/docs/intro#running-the-example-test)\n-\n-## Installing Playwright Pytest[​](#installing-playwright-pytest \"Direct link to Installing Playwright Pytest\")\n-\n-Playwright recommends using the official [Playwright Pytest plugin](/python/docs/test-runners) to write end-to-end tests. It provides context isolation, running it on multiple browser configurations out of the box.\n-\n-Get started by installing Playwright and running the example test to see it in action.\n-\n-Install the [Pytest plugin](https://pypi.org/project/pytest-playwright/):\n-\n--   Pip\n--   Poetry\n--   uv\n-\n-```\n-pip install pytest-playwright\n-```\n-\n-```\n-poetry add pytest-playwright\n-```\n-\n-```\n-uv add pytest-playwright\n-```\n-\n-Install the required browsers:\n-\n-```\n-playwright install\n-```\n-\n-## Add Example Test[​](#add-example-test \"Direct link to Add Example Test\")\n-\n-Create a file that follows the `test_` prefix convention, such as `test_example.py`, inside the current working directory or in a sub-directory with the code below. Make sure your test name also follows the `test_` prefix convention.\n-\n-test\\_example.py\n-\n-```\n-import refrom playwright.sync_api import Page, expectdef test_has_title(page: Page):    page.goto(\"https://playwright.dev/\")    # Expect a title \"to contain\" a substring.    expect(page).to_have_title(re.compile(\"Playwright\"))def test_get_started_link(page: Page):    page.goto(\"https://playwright.dev/\")    # Click the get started link.    page.get_by_role(\"link\", name=\"Get started\").click()    # Expects page to have a heading with the name of Installation.    expect(page.get_by_role(\"heading\", name=\"Installation\")).to_be_visible()\n-```\n-\n-## Running the Example Test[​](#running-the-example-test \"Direct link to Running the Example Test\")\n-\n-By default tests will be run on chromium. This can be configured via the [CLI options](/python/docs/running-tests). Tests are run in headless mode meaning no browser UI will open up when running the tests. Results of the tests and test logs will be shown in the terminal.\n-\n-```\n-pytest\n-```\n-\n-## Updating Playwright[​](#updating-playwright \"Direct link to Updating Playwright\")\n-\n-To update Playwright to the latest version run the following command:\n-\n--   pip\n--   Poetry\n--   uv\n-\n-```\n-pip install pytest-playwright playwright -U\n-```\n-\n-```\n-poetry update pytest-playwright playwright\n-```\n-\n-```\n-uv add --upgrade pytest-playwright playwright\n-```\n-\n-## System requirements[​](#system-requirements \"Direct link to System requirements\")\n-\n--   Python 3.8 or higher.\n--   Windows 11+, Windows Server 2019+ or Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL).\n--   macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later.\n--   Debian 12 / 13, Ubuntu 22.04 / 24.04 / 26.04 (x86-64 or arm64).\n-\n-## Plugin Reference\n-\n-## Introduction[​](#introduction \"Direct link to Introduction\")\n-\n-Playwright provides a [Pytest](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/) plugin to write end-to-end tests. To get started with it, refer to the [getting started guide](/python/docs/intro).\n-\n-## Usage[​](#usage \"Direct link to Usage\")\n-\n-To run your tests, use [Pytest](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/) CLI.\n-\n-```\n-pytest --browser webkit --headed\n-```\n-\n-If you want to add the CLI arguments automatically without specifying them, you can use the [pytest.ini](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/reference.html#ini-options-ref) file:\n-\n-```\n-# content of pytest.ini[pytest]# Run firefox with UIaddopts = --headed --browser firefox\n-```\n-\n-## CLI arguments[​](#cli-arguments \"Direct link to CLI arguments\")\n-\n-Note that CLI arguments are only applied to the default `browser`, `context` and `page` fixtures. If you create a browser, a context or a page with the API call like [browser.new\\_context()](/python/docs/api/class-browser#browser-new-context), the CLI arguments are not applied.\n-\n--   `--headed`: Run tests in headed mode (default: headless).\n--   `--browser`: Run tests in a different browser `chromium`, `firefox`, or `webkit`. It can be specified multiple times (default: `chromium`).\n--   `--browser-channel` [Browser channel](/python/docs/browsers) to be used.\n--   `--slowmo` Slows down Playwright operations by the specified amount of milliseconds. Useful so that you can see what is going on (default: 0).\n--   `--device` [Device](/python/docs/emulation) to be emulated.\n--   `--output` Directory for artifacts produced by tests (default: `test-results`).\n--   `--tracing` Whether to record a [trace](/python/docs/trace-viewer) for each test. `on`, `off`, or `retain-on-failure` (default: `off`).\n--   `--video` Whether to record video for each test. `on`, `off`, or `retain-on-failure` (default: `off`).\n--   `--screenshot` Whether to automatically capture a screenshot after each test. `on`, `off`, or `only-on-failure` (default: `off`).\n--   `--full-page-screenshot` Whether to take a full page screenshot on failure. By default, only the viewport is captured. Requires `--screenshot` to be enabled (default: `off`).\n-\n-## Fixtures[​](#fixtures \"Direct link to Fixtures\")\n-\n-This plugin configures Playwright-specific [fixtures for pytest](https://docs.pytest.org/en/latest/fixture.html). To use these fixtures, use the fixture name as an argument to the test function.\n-\n-```\n-def test_my_app_is_working(fixture_name):    pass    # Test using fixture_name    # ...\n-```\n-\n-**Function scope**: These fixtures are created when requested in a test function and destroyed when the test ends.\n-\n--   `context`: New [browser context](/python/docs/browser-contexts) for a test.\n--   `page`: New [browser page](/python/docs/pages) for a test.\n--   `new_context`: Allows creating different [browser contexts](/python/docs/browser-contexts) for a test. Useful for multi-user scenarios. Accepts the same parameters as [browser.new\\_context()](/python/docs/api/class-browser#browser-new-context).\n-\n-**Session scope**: These fixtures are created when requested in a test function and destroyed when all tests end.\n-\n--   `playwright`: [Playwright](/python/docs/api/class-playwright) instance.\n--   `browser_type`: [BrowserType](/python/docs/api/class-browsertype) instance of the current browser.\n--   `browser`: [Browser](/python/docs/api/class-browser) instance launched by Playwright.\n--   `browser_name`: Browser name as string.\n--   `browser_channel`: Browser channel as string.\n--   `is_chromium`, `is_webkit`, `is_firefox`: Booleans for the respective browser types.\n-\n-**Customizing fixture options**: For `browser` and `context` fixtures, use the following fixtures to define custom launch options.\n-\n--   `browser_type_launch_args`: Override launch arguments for [browser\\_type.launch()](/python/docs/api/class-browsertype#browser-type-launch). It should return a Dict.\n--   `browser_context_args`: Override the options for [browser.new\\_context()](/python/docs/api/class-browser#browser-new-context). It should return a Dict.\n--   `connect_options`: Connect to an existing browser via WebSocket endpoint. It should return a Dict with [browser\\_type.connect()](/python/docs/api/class-browsertype#browser-type-connect) options.\n-\n-Its also possible to override the context options ([browser.new\\_context()](/python/docs/api/class-browser#browser-new-context)) for a single test by using the `browser_context_args` marker:\n-\n-```\n-import pytest@pytest.mark.browser_context_args(timezone_id=\"Europe/Berlin\", locale=\"en-GB\")def test_browser_context_args(page):    assert page.evaluate(\"window.navigator.userAgent\") == \"Europe/Berlin\"    assert page.evaluate(\"window.navigator.languages\") == [\"de-DE\"]\n-```\n-\n-## Parallelism: Running Multiple Tests at Once[​](#parallelism-running-multiple-tests-at-once \"Direct link to Parallelism: Running Multiple Tests at Once\")\n-\n-If your tests are running on a machine with a lot of CPUs, you can speed up the overall execution time of your test suite by using [`pytest-xdist`](https://pypi.org/project/pytest-xdist/) to run multiple tests at once:\n-\n-```\n-# install dependencypip install pytest-xdist# use the --numprocesses flagpytest --numprocesses auto\n-```\n-\n-Depending on the hardware and nature of your tests, you can set `numprocesses` to be anywhere from `2` to the number of CPUs on the machine. If set too high, you may notice unexpected behavior.\n-\n-See [Running Tests](/python/docs/running-tests) for general information on `pytest` options.\n-\n-## Examples[​](#examples \"Direct link to Examples\")\n-\n-### Configure typings for auto-completion[​](#configure-typings-for-auto-completion \"Direct link to Configure typings for auto-completion\")\n-\n-test\\_my\\_application.py\n-\n-```\n-from playwright.sync_api import Pagedef test_visit_admin_dashboard(page: Page):    page.goto(\"/admin\")    # ...\n-```\n-\n-If you're using VSCode with Pylance, these types can be inferred by enabling the `python.testing.pytestEnabled` setting so you don't need the type annotation.\n-\n-### Using multiple contexts[​](#using-multiple-contexts \"Direct link to Using multiple contexts\")\n-\n-In order to simulate multiple users, you can create multiple [`BrowserContext`](/python/docs/browser-contexts) instances.\n-\n-test\\_my\\_application.py\n-\n-```\n-from playwright.sync_api import Page, BrowserContextfrom pytest_playwright.pytest_playwright import CreateContextCallbackdef test_foo(page: Page, new_context: CreateContextCallback) -> None:    page.goto(\"https://example.com\")    context = new_context()    page2 = context.new_page()    # page and page2 are in different contexts\n-```\n-\n-### Skip test by browser[​](#skip-test-by-browser \"Direct link to Skip test by browser\")\n-\n-test\\_my\\_application.py\n-\n-```\n-import pytest@pytest.mark.skip_browser(\"firefox\")def test_visit_example(page):    page.goto(\"https://example.com\")    # ...\n-```\n-\n-### Run on a specific browser[​](#run-on-a-specific-browser \"Direct link to Run on a specific browser\")\n-\n-conftest.py\n-\n-```\n-import pytest@pytest.mark.only_browser(\"chromium\")def test_visit_example(page):    page.goto(\"https://example.com\")    # ...\n-```\n-\n-### Run with a custom browser channel like Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge[​](#run-with-a-custom-browser-channel-like-google-chrome-or-microsoft-edge \"Direct link to Run with a custom browser channel like Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge\")\n-\n-```\n-pytest --browser-channel chrome\n-```\n-\n-test\\_my\\_application.py\n-\n-```\n-def test_example(page):    page.goto(\"https://example.com\")\n-```\n-\n-### Configure base-url[​](#configure-base-url \"Direct link to Configure base-url\")\n-\n-Start Pytest with the `base-url` argument. The [`pytest-base-url`](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-base-url) plugin is used for that which allows you to set the base url from the config, CLI arg or as a fixture.\n-\n-```\n-pytest --base-url http://localhost:8080\n-```\n-\n-test\\_my\\_application.py\n-\n-```\n-def test_visit_example(page):    page.goto(\"/admin\")    # -> Will result in http://localhost:8080/admin\n-```\n-\n-### Ignore HTTPS errors[​](#ignore-https-errors \"Direct link to Ignore HTTPS errors\")\n-\n-conftest.py\n-\n-```\n-import pytest@pytest.fixture(scope=\"session\")def browser_context_args(browser_context_args):    return {        **browser_context_args,        \"ignore_https_errors\": True    }\n-```\n-\n-### Use custom viewport size[​](#use-custom-viewport-size \"Direct link to Use custom viewport size\")\n-\n-conftest.py\n-\n-```\n-import pytest@pytest.fixture(scope=\"session\")def browser_context_args(browser_context_args):    return {        **browser_context_args,        \"viewport\": {            \"width\": 1920,            \"height\": 1080,        }    }\n-```\n-\n-### Device emulation / BrowserContext option overrides[​](#device-emulation--browsercontext-option-overrides \"Direct link to Device emulation / BrowserContext option overrides\")\n-\n-conftest.py\n-\n-```\n-import pytest@pytest.fixture(scope=\"session\")def browser_context_args(browser_context_args, playwright):    iphone_11 = playwright.devices['iPhone 11 Pro']    return {        **browser_context_args,        **iphone_11,    }\n-```\n-\n-Or via the CLI `--device=\"iPhone 11 Pro\"`\n-\n-### Connect to remote browsers[​](#connect-to-remote-browsers \"Direct link to Connect to remote browsers\")\n-\n-conftest.py\n-\n-```\n-import pytest@pytest.fixture(scope=\"session\")def connect_options():    return {        \"wsEndpoint\": \"ws://localhost:8080/ws\"    }\n-```\n-\n-### Using with `unittest.TestCase`[​](#using-with-unittesttestcase \"Direct link to using-with-unittesttestcase\")\n-\n-See the following example for using it with `unittest.TestCase`. This has a limitation, that only a single browser can be specified and no matrix of multiple browsers gets generated when specifying multiple.\n-\n-```\n-import pytestimport unittestfrom playwright.sync_api import Pageclass MyTest(unittest.TestCase):    @pytest.fixture(autouse=True)    def setup(self, page: Page):        self.page = page    def test_foobar(self):        self.page.goto(\"https://microsoft.com\")        self.page.locator(\"#foobar\").click()        assert self.page.evaluate(\"1 + 1\") == 2\n-```\n-\n-## Debugging[​](#debugging \"Direct link to Debugging\")\n-\n-### Use with pdb[​](#use-with-pdb \"Direct link to Use with pdb\")\n-\n-Use the `breakpoint()` statement in your test code to pause execution and get a [pdb](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pdb.html) REPL.\n-\n-```\n-def test_bing_is_working(page):    page.goto(\"https://bing.com\")    breakpoint()    # ...\n-```\n-\n-## Deploy to CI[​](#deploy-to-ci \"Direct link to Deploy to CI\")\n-\n-See the [guides for CI providers](/python/docs/ci) to deploy your tests to CI/CD.\n-\n-## Async Fixtures[​](#async-fixtures \"Direct link to Async Fixtures\")\n-\n-To use async fixtures, install [`pytest-playwright-asyncio`](https://pypi.org/project/pytest-playwright-asyncio/).\n-\n-Ensure you are using `pytest-asyncio>=0.26.0` and set [`asyncio_default_test_loop_scope = session`](https://pytest-asyncio.readthedocs.io/en/v0.26.0/how-to-guides/change_default_test_loop.html) in your configuration (`pytest.ini/pyproject.toml/setup.cfg`).\n-\n-```\n-import pytestfrom playwright.async_api import Page@pytest.mark.asyncio(loop_scope=\"session\")async def test_foo(page: Page):    await page.goto(\"https://github.com\")    # ...\n-```\n-\n-[\n-\n-Previous\n-\n-Setting up CI\n-\n-](/python/docs/ci-intro)[\n-\n-Next\n-\n-Getting started - Library\n-\n-](/python/docs/library)\n-\n-- Continuous Integration\n-\n-## Introduction[​](#introduction \"Direct link to Introduction\")\n-\n-Playwright tests can be executed in CI environments. We have created sample configurations for common CI providers.\n-\n-3 steps to get your tests running on CI:\n-\n-1.  **Ensure CI agent can run browsers**: Use [our Docker image](/python/docs/docker) in Linux agents or install your dependencies using the [CLI](/python/docs/browsers#install-system-dependencies).\n-    \n-2.  **Install Playwright**:\n-    \n-    ```\n-    pip install playwrightplaywright install --with-deps\n-    ```\n-    \n-3.  **Run your tests**:\n-    \n-    ```\n-    pytest\n-    ```\n-    \n-\n-## CI configurations[​](#ci-configurations \"Direct link to CI configurations\")\n-\n-The [Command line tools](/python/docs/browsers#install-system-dependencies) can be used to install all operating system dependencies in CI.\n-\n-### GitHub Actions[​](#github-actions \"Direct link to GitHub Actions\")\n-\n-#### On push/pull\\_request[​](#on-pushpull_request \"Direct link to On push/pull_request\")\n-\n-Tests will run on push or pull request on branches main/master. The [workflow](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/about-workflows) will install all dependencies, install Playwright and then run the tests.\n-\n-.github/workflows/playwright.yml\n-\n-```\n-name: Playwright Testson:  push:    branches: [ main, master ]  pull_request:    branches: [ main, master ]jobs:  test:    timeout-minutes: 60    runs-on: ubuntu-latest    steps:    - uses: actions/checkout@v6    - name: Set up Python      uses: actions/setup-python@v6      with:        python-version: '3.13'    - name: Install dependencies      run: |        python -m pip install --upgrade pip        pip install -r requirements.txt    - name: Ensure browsers are installed      run: python -m playwright install --with-deps    - name: Run your tests      run: pytest --tracing=retain-on-failure    - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v5      if: ${{ !cancelled() }}      with:        name: playwright-traces        path: test-results/\n-```\n-\n-#### Via Containers[​](#via-containers \"Direct link to Via Containers\")\n-\n-GitHub Actions support [running jobs in a container](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-jobs/running-jobs-in-a-container) by using the [`jobs.<job_id>.container`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/workflow-syntax-for-github-actions#jobsjob_idcontainer) option. This is useful to not pollute the host environment with dependencies and to have a consistent environment for e.g. screenshots/visual regression testing across different operating systems.\n-\n-.github/workflows/playwright.yml\n-\n-```\n-name: Playwright Testson:  push:    branches: [ main, master ]  pull_request:    branches: [ main, master ]jobs:  playwright:    name: 'Playwright Tests'    runs-on: ubuntu-latest    container:      image: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright/python:v1.62.0-noble      options: --user 1001    steps:      - uses: actions/checkout@v6      - name: Set up Python        uses: actions/setup-python@v6        with:          python-version: '3.13'      - name: Install dependencies        run: |          python -m pip install --upgrade pip          pip install -r local-requirements.txt          pip install -e .      - name: Run your tests        run: pytest\n-```\n-\n-#### On deployment[​](#on-deployment \"Direct link to On deployment\")\n-\n-This will start the tests after a [GitHub Deployment](https://developer.github.com/v3/repos/deployments/) went into the `success` state. Services like Vercel use this pattern so you can run your end-to-end tests on their deployed environment.\n-\n-.github/workflows/playwright.yml\n-\n-```\n-name: Playwright Testson:  deployment_status:jobs:  test:    timeout-minutes: 60    runs-on: ubuntu-latest    if: github.event.deployment_status.state == 'success'    steps:    - uses: actions/checkout@v6      uses: actions/setup-python@v6      with:        python-version: '3.13'    - name: Install dependencies      run: |        python -m pip install --upgrade pip        pip install -r requirements.txt    - name: Ensure browsers are installed      run: python -m playwright install --with-deps    - name: Run tests      run: pytest      env:        # This might depend on your test-runner        PLAYWRIGHT_TEST_BASE_URL: ${{ github.event.deployment_status.target_url }}\n-```\n-\n-### Docker[​](#docker \"Direct link to Docker\")\n-\n-We have a [pre-built Docker image](/python/docs/docker) which can either be used directly or as a reference to update your existing Docker definitions. Make sure to follow the [Recommended Docker Configuration](/python/docs/docker#recommended-docker-configuration) to ensure the best performance.\n-\n-### Azure Pipelines[​](#azure-pipelines \"Direct link to Azure Pipelines\")\n-\n-For Windows or macOS agents, no additional configuration is required, just install Playwright and run your tests.\n-\n-For Linux agents, you can use [our Docker container](/python/docs/docker) with Azure Pipelines support [running containerized jobs](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/process/container-phases?view=azure-devops). Alternatively, you can use [Command line tools](/python/docs/browsers#install-system-dependencies) to install all necessary dependencies.\n-\n-For running the Playwright tests use this pipeline task:\n-\n-```\n-trigger:- mainpool:  vmImage: ubuntu-lateststeps:- task: UsePythonVersion@0  inputs:    versionSpec: '3.13'  displayName: 'Use Python'- script: |    python -m pip install --upgrade pip    pip install -r requirements.txt  displayName: 'Install dependencies'- script: playwright install --with-deps  displayName: 'Install Playwright browsers'- script: pytest  displayName: 'Run Playwright tests'\n-```\n-\n-#### Azure Pipelines (containerized)[​](#azure-pipelines-containerized \"Direct link to Azure Pipelines (containerized)\")\n-\n-```\n-trigger:- mainpool:  vmImage: ubuntu-latestcontainer: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright/python:v1.62.0-noblesteps:- task: UsePythonVersion@0  inputs:    versionSpec: '3.13'  displayName: 'Use Python'- script: |    python -m pip install --upgrade pip    pip install -r requirements.txt  displayName: 'Install dependencies'- script: pytest  displayName: 'Run tests'\n-```\n-\n-### CircleCI[​](#circleci \"Direct link to CircleCI\")\n-\n-Running Playwright on CircleCI is very similar to running on GitHub Actions. In order to specify the pre-built Playwright [Docker image](/python/docs/docker), simply modify the agent definition with `docker:` in your config like so:\n-\n-```\n-executors:  pw-noble-development:    docker:      - image: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright/python:v1.62.0-noble\n-```\n-\n-Note: When using the docker agent definition, you are specifying the resource class of where playwright runs to the 'medium' tier [here](https://circleci.com/docs/configuration-reference?#docker-execution-environment). The default behavior of Playwright is to set the number of workers to the detected core count (2 in the case of the medium tier). Overriding the number of workers to greater than this number will cause unnecessary timeouts and failures.\n-\n-### Jenkins[​](#jenkins \"Direct link to Jenkins\")\n-\n-Jenkins supports Docker agents for pipelines. Use the [Playwright Docker image](/python/docs/docker) to run tests on Jenkins.\n-\n-```\n-pipeline {   agent { docker { image 'mcr.microsoft.com/playwright/python:v1.62.0-noble' } }   stages {      stage('e2e-tests') {         steps {            sh 'pip install -r requirements.txt'            sh 'pytest'         }      }   }}\n-```\n-\n-### Bitbucket Pipelines[​](#bitbucket-pipelines \"Direct link to Bitbucket Pipelines\")\n-\n-Bitbucket Pipelines can use public [Docker images as build environments](https://confluence.atlassian.com/bitbucket/use-docker-images-as-build-environments-792298897.html). To run Playwright tests on Bitbucket, use our public Docker image ([see Dockerfile](/python/docs/docker)).\n-\n-```\n-image: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright/python:v1.62.0-noble\n-```\n-\n-### GitLab CI[​](#gitlab-ci \"Direct link to GitLab CI\")\n-\n-To run Playwright tests on GitLab, use our public Docker image ([see Dockerfile](/python/docs/docker)).\n-\n-```\n-stages:  - testtests:  stage: test  image: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright/python:v1.62.0-noble  script:  ...\n-```\n-\n-## Caching browsers[​](#caching-browsers \"Direct link to Caching browsers\")\n-\n-Caching browser binaries is not recommended, since the amount of time it takes to restore the cache is comparable to the time it takes to download the binaries. Especially under Linux, [operating system dependencies](/python/docs/browsers#install-system-dependencies) need to be installed, which are not cacheable.\n-\n-If you still want to cache the browser binaries between CI runs, cache [these directories](/python/docs/browsers#managing-browser-binaries) in your CI configuration, against a hash of the Playwright version.\n-\n-## Debugging browser launches[​](#debugging-browser-launches \"Direct link to Debugging browser launches\")\n-\n-Playwright supports the `DEBUG` environment variable to output debug logs during execution. Setting it to `pw:browser` is helpful while debugging `Error: Failed to launch browser` errors.\n-\n-```\n-DEBUG=pw:browser pytest\n-```\n-\n-## Running headed[​](#running-headed \"Direct link to Running headed\")\n-\n-By default, Playwright launches browsers in headless mode. See in our [Running tests](/python/docs/running-tests#run-tests-in-headed-mode) guide how to run tests in headed mode.\n-\n-On Linux agents, headed execution requires [Xvfb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xvfb) to be installed. Our [Docker image](/python/docs/docker) and GitHub Action have Xvfb pre-installed. To run browsers in headed mode with Xvfb, add `xvfb-run` before the actual command.\n-\n-```\n-xvfb-run pytest\n-```\n-\n-[\n-\n-Previous\n-\n-Docker\n-\n-](/python/docs/docker)[\n-\n-Next\n-\n-Selenium Grid (experimental)\n-\n-](/python/docs/selenium-grid)\n-\n--   [Introduction](#introduction)\n-- Neither file has been created yet.\n-\n----\n-\n-# `MVP-PLAN.md` — Finalized specification\n-\n-## 1. Product objective\n-\n-Build a local browser application that estimates:\n-\n-- Whether a user-selected stock or ETF will rise or fall.\n-- The probability of specified percentage moves.\n-- The plausible magnitude of the move by a clearly identified target close.\n-\n-Use the most recent eligible Yahoo Finance data, preserve each forecast, and support comparison with subsequent outcomes.\n-\n-### Required capabilities\n-\n-1. Search by company name or ticker and switch instruments freely.\n-2. Calculate **close-to-close** and **intraday-to-close** forecasts.\n-3. Display probabilities, prediction intervals, conditional gains/losses, and historical charts.\n-4. Show reference price, data timestamp, target session, freshness, and sample size.\n-5. Preserve every submitted search and analysis, including failures and repeated requests.\n-6. Search, filter, reopen, and export that history.\n-7. Store historical market data and immutable forecast inputs.\n-8. Back up and restore the database.\n-9. Pass automated browser acceptance tests.\n-10. Provide reproducible setup, documentation, CI, and published Git revisions.\n-\n-**A daily-only implementation is an intermediate checkpoint. MVP completion requires both forecast modes.**\n-\n-## 2. Architecture\n-\n-```text\n-Browser frontend\n-    │ HTTP / JSON\n-    ▼\n-FastAPI /api/v1/*\n-    │\n-    ▼\n-Application services\n-    ├── Yahoo Finance adapter\n-    ├── Forecasting and evaluation\n-    └── Database repository\n-            │\n-            ▼\n-          SQLite\n-```\n-\n-All frontend application data must pass through the API. Database connections, SQL, filesystem paths, and backup operations belong to the backend.\n-\n-### Stack\n-\n-- Python 3.11-compatible application.\n-- FastAPI with one Uvicorn worker.\n-- Jinja2 for page shells; CSS and small JavaScript modules.\n-- Locally served Chart.js.\n-- yfinance, NumPy/pandas, and exchange calendars.\n-- Built-in `sqlite3` with versioned migrations.\n-- `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`.\n-- pytest, Ruff, mypy, Playwright, and `pytest-playwright`.\n-\n-### API surface\n-\n-- `POST /api/v1/searches`\n-- `POST /api/v1/forecasts`\n-- `GET /api/v1/forecasts/{id}`\n-- `GET /api/v1/history`\n-- `GET /api/v1/instruments/{id}/prices`\n-- `GET /api/v1/exports`\n-- `GET /api/v1/backups/status`\n-\n-Responses will have validated schemas, bounded pagination, and consistent errors.\n-\n-## 3. Market data and forecasting\n-\n-### Daily mode\n-\n-Use the latest completed session to forecast the next session’s close.\n-\n-Implement a historical-frequency baseline and a volatility-adjusted historical distribution. Derive direction probabilities, thresholds, and intervals consistently from the chosen distribution.\n-\n-### Intraday mode\n-\n-Use the latest eligible completed five-minute bar to forecast the upcoming regular-session close.\n-\n-Use comparable historical intraday cutoffs and evaluate by trading session. Archive retrieved bars because Yahoo’s five-minute history is limited to approximately 60 calendar days.\n-\n-### Data correctness\n-\n-- Distinguish market-observation time from download time.\n-- Exclude incomplete bars from completed-period calculations.\n-- Handle exchange calendars, holidays, early closes, and timezones.\n-- Handle splits and currency units consistently.\n-- Keep price-return and dividend-adjusted total-return definitions explicit.\n-- Avoid treating missing-session gaps as ordinary one-session returns.\n-- Record stale data and insufficient-history conditions explicitly.\n-- Preserve original forecasts when Yahoo revises historical data.\n-\n-Historical reconstructions and forecasts actually saved at the time must have distinct labels.\n-\n-### Model acceptance\n-\n-- Walk-forward evaluation with chronological train/evaluation boundaries.\n-- No future observations in historical predictions.\n-- Comparison against simple baselines.\n-- Probability scoring, reliability plots, and interval coverage.\n-- Counts and uncertainty for rare events.\n-- Documented model/configuration versions.\n-\n-Acceptance demonstrates correct calculations and honest evaluation; it does not assume a predetermined prediction accuracy.\n-\n-## 4. Storage and backups\n-\n-SQLite will contain:\n-\n-- Instruments and exchange metadata.\n-- Daily/intraday market bars.\n-- Submitted queries and their statuses.\n-- Immutable, deduplicated input snapshots.\n-- Forecast results and model versions.\n-- Subsequent outcomes and evaluation results.\n-\n-History will use indexed filters and full-text search. Saved results must remain readable offline.\n-\n-Use short explicit transactions, foreign keys, thread-owned connections, and a busy timeout. Start with rollback-journal mode, appropriate to this workload and the installed SQLite version.\n-\n-Backups must:\n-- Use SQLite’s backup API.\n-- Run when due and before migrations.\n-- Be integrity-checked.\n-- Have configurable retention and storage limits.\n-- Support restoration while the application is stopped.\n-- Preserve searchable queries and original forecasts after restoration.\n-\n-Application history has no automatic expiry.\n-\n-## 5. Frontend acceptance\n-\n-The dashboard must provide:\n-\n-- Company/ticker selection with exchange and currency.\n-- Forecast-mode and historical-cutoff controls.\n-- Up/down/unchanged probabilities.\n-- Configurable movement thresholds.\n-- Median and conditional moves.\n-- Prediction intervals.\n-- Historical-price and return-distribution charts.\n-- Searchable query history and original-result views.\n-- CSV/JSON exports and backup status.\n-- Loading, error, stale-data, and insufficient-history states.\n-\n-Acceptance includes keyboard operation, readable contrast, responsive layouts, and numerical summaries for charts.\n-\n-## 6. Mandatory Playwright setup\n-\n-### Browser configuration\n-\n-- Use **Playwright for Python** with `pytest-playwright`.\n-- Run Chromium headlessly.\n-- Install the headless shell to reduce download/storage requirements.\n-- Run tests serially on the laptop.\n-- Isolate browser contexts and test databases.\n-- Retain traces and screenshots on failure.\n-- Keep video recording disabled by default.\n-- Pin Playwright dependencies and install their matching browser revision.\n-\n-Proposed commands, to be established during implementation:\n-\n-```bash\n-uv sync --locked\n-uv run playwright install --with-deps --only-shell chromium\n-\n-uv run pytest tests/browser -q \\\n-  --browser chromium \\\n-  --tracing retain-on-failure \\\n-  --screenshot only-on-failure \\\n-  --output .artifacts/playwright\n-```\n-\n-Headless execution is Playwright’s default. The documented pytest options support the proposed failure artifacts.[2][3]\n-\n-### End-to-end test architecture\n-\n-```text\n-Headless browser\n-    → real running application\n-    → real API\n-    → real application services\n-    → real temporary SQLite database\n-```\n-\n-For repeatable acceptance tests, substitute controlled data **at the Yahoo provider boundary**. Forecasting, API responses, persistence, and frontend behavior remain real.\n-\n-Fixtures will start the server, wait for readiness, provide an isolated database, and clean up processes afterward.\n-\n-A separate live smoke suite will exercise the real Yahoo adapter through the UI. Successful live verification is required for final acceptance. Provider outages remain recorded blockers for that gate.\n-\n-### Required browser scenarios\n-\n-| ID | Acceptance scenario |\n-|---|---|\n-| B01 | Search by company name and select the intended instrument |\n-| B02 | Switch between multiple symbols without mixing their data |\n-| B03 | Complete a daily forecast and verify displayed values against the API result |\n-| B04 | Complete an intraday forecast with the correct reference and target timestamps |\n-| B05 | Display thresholds, intervals, and populated charts |\n-| B06 | Submit a historical reconstruction and identify it correctly |\n-| B07 | Find successful, failed, and repeated queries in history |\n-| B08 | Restart the application and reopen the original saved forecast |\n-| B09 | Refresh market data without changing an earlier saved forecast |\n-| B10 | Handle invalid symbols, missing data, rate limits, and stale data |\n-| B11 | Download and validate CSV/JSON exports |\n-| B12 | Restore a backup, restart the app, and retrieve restored history |\n-| B13 | Operate core controls using the keyboard and at narrow viewport widths |\n-| B14 | Verify application-data requests use the API and database files are inaccessible |\n-| B15 | Complete a live Yahoo search → forecast → history journey |\n-| B16 | Verify controlled-data operation has no unexpected external dependencies or uncaught browser errors |\n-\n-A visible page or screenshot alone does not satisfy functional acceptance. Tests must assert the expected behavior and persisted results.\n-\n-Required acceptance tests cannot be silently skipped or marked as expected failures.\n-\n-## 7. Security and resource requirements\n-\n-- Bind to loopback by default.\n-- Validate Host/Origin and protect state-changing requests.\n-- Use parameterized SQL and allowlisted sorting.\n-- Validate symbols, dates, thresholds, and request sizes.\n-- Escape provider/user text in the frontend.\n-- Use a restrictive Content Security Policy.\n-- Keep databases, backups, logs, secrets, and provider caches outside public paths.\n-- Sanitize spreadsheet exports.\n-- Run dependency vulnerability checks.\n-- Keep restore operations in the local CLI.\n-\n-Measure these proposed laptop targets:\n-- Normal application-server memory below 500 MiB.\n-- Cached single-symbol analysis below one second.\n-- Indexed history search below 250 ms on a 100,000-query fixture.\n-- Negligible background CPU use while idle.\n-\n-Measure browser-test resource usage separately from server runtime.\n-\n-## 8. Development and release gates\n-\n-Provide these task-runner commands:\n-\n-| Command | Responsibility |\n-|---|---|\n-| `make setup` | Reproducible development dependency installation |\n-| `make browser-install` | Install Chromium headless shell and required libraries |\n-| `make dev` | Start the local application |\n-| `make check` | Format check, lint, typecheck, unit/API tests |\n-| `make browser-test` | Deterministic Playwright acceptance suite |\n-| `make acceptance` | Complete deterministic acceptance, including browser and restore tests |\n-| `make live-smoke` | Explicit real-Yahoo browser verification |\n-| `make release-check` | Acceptance, security audit, performance evidence, and requirement review |\n-\n-GitHub Actions will run deterministic checks and browser tests on pushes and pull requests. Failed runs will retain bounded diagnostic artifacts.\n-\n-Each checkpoint requires:\n-1. Relevant checks passing.\n-2. Diff and tracked-file review.\n-3. An intentional commit.\n-4. Each value is a local path, Git repository, or string shorthand.\n-- `agent` is an object keyed by agent name, not an array.\n-- `command` is an object keyed by command name, not an array.\n-- `plugin` is an array of strings or `[name, options]` tuples, not an object.\n-- `mcp[name].command` is an array of strings, never a single string. `type` is required.\n-- `permission` is either a string action or an object keyed by tool name.\n-\n-## Skills\n-\n-opencode's skill loader scans for `**/SKILL.md` inside skill directories. The\n-file is named `SKILL.md` exactly, and lives in its own folder named after the\n-skill:\n-\n-```\n-.opencode/skills/my-skill/SKILL.md\n-```\n-\n-Frontmatter:\n-\n-```markdown\n----\n-name: my-skill\n-description: One sentence covering what this skill does AND when to trigger it. Front-load the literal keywords or filenames the user is likely to say.\n----\n-\n-# My Skill\n-\n-(skill body in markdown: instructions, examples, references)\n-```\n-\n-- `name` is required, lowercase hyphen-separated, up to 64 chars, and matches the folder name.\n-- `description` is effectively required: skills without one are filtered out and never surfaced to the model. Cover both _what_ the skill does and _when_ to use it. Write in third person (\"Use when...\", not \"I help with...\"). Front-load concrete trigger keywords and filenames; gate with \"Use ONLY when...\" if the skill should stay quiet on adjacent topics.\n-- Optional: `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata` (string-string map).\n-\n-Register skills from non-default locations via `skills.paths` (scanned\n-recursively for `**/SKILL.md`) and `skills.urls` (each URL serves a list of\n-skills).\n-\n-## References\n-\n-References make local directories and Git repositories outside the active\n-project available as supporting context. Configure them under `references`,\n-keyed by the alias used in `@` autocomplete:\n-\n-```json\n-{\n-  \"references\": {\n-    \"docs\": {\n-      \"path\": \"../product-docs\",\n-      \"description\": \"Use for product behavior and terminology\"\n-    },\n-    \"effect\": {\n-      \"repository\": \"Effect-TS/effect\",\n-      \"branch\": \"main\",\n-      \"description\": \"Use for Effect implementation details\"\n-    }\n-  }\n-}\n-```\n-\n-Local `path` values may be relative to the declaring config, absolute, or use\n-`~/`. Git `repository` values accept Git URLs, host/path references, and GitHub\n-`owner/repo` shorthand; `branch` is optional. Both forms support optional\n-`description` and `hidden` fields.\n-\n-- Only references with a `description` are advertised to agents in system context.\n-- `hidden: true` removes a reference from TUI `@` autocomplete only. It remains available to agents and by direct path.\n-- Reference directories are automatically allowed through the external-directory boundary; normal read/edit/tool permissions still apply.\n-- String shorthand is supported: use `\"docs\": \"../docs\"` for local paths or `\"effect\": \"Effect-TS/effect\"` for Git repositories.\n-\n-## Agents\n-\n-Two ways to define an agent. Use the file form for anything non-trivial.\n-\n-### Inline (in `opencode.json`)\n-\n-```json\n-{\n-  \"agent\": {\n-    \"my-reviewer\": {\n-      \"description\": \"Reviews PRs for style violations.\",\n-      \"mode\": \"subagent\",\n-      \"model\": \"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6\",\n-      \"permission\": { \"edit\": \"deny\", \"bash\": \"ask\" },\n-      \"prompt\": \"You are a strict PR reviewer...\"\n-    }\n-  }\n-}\n-```\n-\n-### File\n-\n-```\n-.opencode/agent/my-reviewer.md      OR     .opencode/agents/my-reviewer.md\n-```\n-\n-```markdown\n----\n-description: Reviews PRs for style violations.\n-mode: subagent\n-model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6\n-permission:\n-  edit: deny\n-  bash: ask\n----\n-\n-You are a strict PR reviewer. Focus on...\n-```\n-\n-The file body becomes the agent's `prompt`. Do not also put `prompt:` in the\n-frontmatter.\n-\n-`mode` is one of `\"primary\"`, `\"subagent\"`, `\"all\"`.\n-\n-Allowed top-level frontmatter fields: `name, model, variant, description, mode,\n-hidden, color, steps, options, permission, disable, temperature, top_p`. Any\n-unknown field is silently routed into `options`.\n-\n-To disable a built-in agent: `agent: { build: { disable: true } }`, or in a\n-file, `disable: true` in frontmatter.\n-\n-`default_agent` must point to a non-hidden, primary-mode agent.\n-\n-### Built-in agents\n-\n-opencode ships with `build`, `plan`, `general`, `explore`. Hidden internal agents:\n-`compaction`, `title`, `summary`. To override a built-in's fields, define the\n-same key in `agent: { <name>: { ... } }`.\n-\n-## Commands\n-\n-opencode's command loader scans for `**/*.md` inside command directories. The\n-file is named after the command, and lives directly inside the `command` folder:\n-\n-```\n-.opencode/command/deploy.md\n-```\n-\n-Frontmatter:\n-\n-```markdown\n----\n-description: One sentence describing what the command does.\n-agent: build\n-model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6\n----\n-\n-(command body in markdown: the prompt opencode runs, with $ARGUMENTS for the user's input)\n-```\n-\n-- `template` is the command body — everything below the frontmatter — and is required: it is the prompt opencode runs when the command is invoked. Do not also put a `template:` key in the frontmatter.\n-- `$ARGUMENTS` is replaced with everything the user typed after the command; `$1`, `$2`, … pull individual positional arguments.\n-- Optional: `description`, `agent`, `model`, `variant`, `subtask`.\n-\n-## Plugins\n-\n-`plugin:` is an array. Each entry is one of:\n-\n-```json\n-\"plugin\": [\n-  \"opencode-gemini-auth\",            // npm spec, latest\n-  \"opencode-foo@1.2.3\",              // npm spec, pinned\n-  \"./local-plugin.ts\",               // file path, relative to the declaring config\n-  \"file:///abs/path/plugin.js\",      // file URL\n-  [\"opencode-bar\", { \"key\": \"val\" }] // tuple form with options\n-]\n-```\n-\n-Auto-discovered plugins (no config entry needed): any `*.ts` or `*.js` file in\n-`.opencode/plugin/` or `.opencode/plugins/`.\n-\n-A plugin module exports `default` (or any named export) of type\n-`Plugin = (input: PluginInput, options?) => Promise<Hooks>`. The export is a\n-function, not a plain object literal, and the function returns an object\n-(return `{}` if there is nothing to register).\n-\n-```ts\n-import type { Plugin } from \"@opencode-ai/plugin\"\n-\n-export default (async ({ client, project, directory, $ }) => {\n-  return {\n-    config: (cfg) => {\n-      // cfg is the live merged config; mutate fields here.\n-    },\n-    \"tool.execute.before\": async (input, output) => {\n-      // mutate output.args before the tool runs\n-    },\n-  }\n-}) satisfies Plugin\n-```\n-\n-Hook surface (mutate `output` in place; return `void`):\n-\n-- `event(input)`: every bus event\n-- `config(cfg)`: once on init with the merged config\n-- `chat.message`, `chat.params`, `chat.headers`\n-- `tool.execute.before`, `tool.execute.after`\n-- `tool.definition`\n-- `command.execute.before`\n-- `shell.env`\n-- `permission.ask`\n-- `experimental.chat.messages.transform`, `experimental.chat.system.transform`,\n-  `experimental.session.compacting`, `experimental.compaction.autocontinue`,\n-  `experimental.text.complete`\n-\n-Special object-shaped (not callbacks): `tool: { my_tool: { ... } }`,\n-`auth: { ... }`, `provider: { ... }`.\n-\n-## MCP servers\n-\n-`mcp:` is an object keyed by server name. Each server is discriminated by\n-`type`:\n-\n-```json\n-{\n-  \"mcp\": {\n-    \"playwright\": {\n-      \"type\": \"local\",\n-      \"command\": [\"npx\", \"-y\", \"@playwright/mcp\"],\n-      \"enabled\": true,\n-      \"environment\": { \"BROWSER\": \"chromium\" }\n-    },\n-    \"github\": {\n-      \"type\": \"remote\",\n-      \"url\": \"https://...\",\n-      \"enabled\": true,\n-      \"headers\": { \"Authorization\": \"Bearer {env:GITHUB_TOKEN}\" }\n-    },\n-    \"old-server\": { \"enabled\": false }\n-  }\n-}\n-```\n-\n-`command` is an array of strings. `environment` sets environment variables for\n-a local MCP server. `type` is required. Use `enabled: false` to\n-disable a server inherited from a parent config. String values such as header\n-tokens support `{env:VAR}` interpolation (and `{file:path}`); the shell-style\n-`${VAR}` is not substituted.\n-\n-## Permissions\n-\n-```json\n-\"permission\": {\n-  \"edit\": \"deny\",\n-  \"bash\": { \"git *\": \"allow\", \"rm *\": \"deny\", \"*\": \"ask\" },\n-  \"external_directory\": { \"~/secrets/**\": \"deny\", \"*\": \"allow\" }\n-}\n-```\n-\n-Actions: `\"allow\"`, `\"ask\"`, `\"deny\"`.\n-\n-Per-tool value forms: `\"allow\"` shorthand (treated as `{\"*\": \"allow\"}`), or an\n-object `{ pattern: action }`. Within an object, **insertion order matters**.\n-opencode evaluates the LAST matching rule, so put broad rules first and narrow\n-rules last.\n-\n-`permission: \"allow\"` (a string at the top level) is shorthand for \"allow\n-everything\" and is rarely what the user wants.\n-\n-Known permission keys: `read, edit, glob, grep, list, bash, task,\n-external_directory, todowrite, question, webfetch, websearch, lsp, doom_loop,\n-skill`. Some of these (`todowrite,\n-question, webfetch, websearch, doom_loop`) only accept a flat\n-action, not a per-pattern object.\n-\n-`external_directory` patterns are filesystem paths (use `~/`, absolute paths,\n-or globs like `~/projects/**`).\n-\n-Per-agent `permission:` overrides top-level `permission:`. Plan Mode lives on\n-the `plan` agent's permission ruleset (`edit: deny *`).\n-\n-## Escape hatches\n-\n-When a user's config is broken and opencode won't start, these env vars help:\n-\n-- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG=1`: skip the project's local `opencode.json`\n-  and start from globals only. Run from the project directory, opencode loads,\n-  the user edits the broken file, then they restart without the flag.\n-- `OPENCODE_CONFIG=/path/to/file.json`: load an additional explicit config.\n-- `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT='{\"$schema\":\"https://opencode.ai/config.json\"}'`:\n-  inject inline JSON as a final local-scope merge.\n-- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS=1`: skip default plugins.\n-- `OPENCODE_PURE=1`: skip external plugins entirely.\n-- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_SKILLS=1`,\n-  `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_SKILLS=1`: skip the external skill scans under\n-  `~/.claude/` and `~/.agents/`.\n-\n-## When proposing edits\n-\n-- Validate against the schema before writing. If you are unsure of a field's\n-  exact shape, or the field is not covered in this skill, fetch\n-  `https://opencode.ai/config.json` and read the schema rather than guessing.\n-- Preserve `$schema` and any existing fields the user did not ask to change.\n-- For agent, command, skill, and plugin definitions, prefer creating new files\n-  in the correct location over inlining everything in `opencode.json`.\n-- If the user's existing config is malformed, point them at the env-var escape\n-  hatches above so they can edit from inside opencode without breaking their\n-  session.\n-- After saving any config change, remind the user to quit and restart opencode\n-  — running sessions keep using the already-loaded config.\n-\n-Base directory for this skill: .\n-Relative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.\n-Note: file list is sampled.\n-\n-<skill_files>\n-<file>/home/eddie/stock_probs/prob_calc_yf.py</file>\n-<file>/home/eddie/stock_probs/prob_calc_hardcoded.py</file>\n-<file>/home/eddie/stock_probs/burry_env/pyvenv.cfg</file>\n-<file>/home/eddie/stock_probs/5%</file>\n-<file>/home/eddie/stock_probs/27.5%</file>\n-<file>/home/eddie/stock_probs/10%</file>\n-<file>/home/eddie/stock_probs/prob_calc.py</file>\n-<file>/home/eddie/stock_probs/burry_env/bin/sample</file>\n-<file>/home/eddie/stock_probs/burry_env/bin/normalizer</file>\n-<file>/home/eddie/stock_probs/burry_env/bin/websockets</file>\n-</skill_files>\n-</skill_content>\n-```\n-\n----\n-\n-## Assistant (Plan · GPT-6 Astra · 16.2s)\n-\n-**Tool: webfetch**\n-\n-**Input:**\n-```json\n-{\n-  \"url\": \"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/playwright-mcp/main/README.md\",\n-  \"format\": \"markdown\"\n-}\n-```\n-\n-**Output:**\n-```\n-## Playwright MCP\n-\n-A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that provides browser automation capabilities using [Playwright](https://playwright.dev). This server enables LLMs to interact with web pages through structured accessibility snapshots, bypassing the need for screenshots or visually-tuned models.\n-\n-### Playwright MCP vs Playwright CLI\n-\n-This package provides MCP interface into Playwright. If you are using a **coding agent**, you might benefit from using the [CLI+SKILLS](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-cli) instead.\n-\n-- **CLI**: Modern **coding agents** increasingly favor CLI–based workflows exposed as SKILLs over MCP because CLI invocations are more token-efficient: they avoid loading large tool schemas and verbose accessibility trees into the model context, allowing agents to act through concise, purpose-built commands. This makes CLI + SKILLs better suited for high-throughput coding agents that must balance browser automation with large codebases, tests, and reasoning within limited context windows.<br>**Learn more about [Playwright CLI with SKILLS](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-cli)**.\n-\n-- **MCP**: MCP remains relevant for specialized agentic loops that benefit from persistent state, rich introspection, and iterative reasoning over page structure, such as exploratory automation, self-healing tests, or long-running autonomous workflows where maintaining continuous browser context outweighs token cost concerns.\n-\n-### Key Features\n-\n-- **Fast and lightweight**. Uses Playwright's accessibility tree, not pixel-based input.\n-- **LLM-friendly**. No vision models needed, operates purely on structured data.\n-- **Deterministic tool application**. Avoids ambiguity common with screenshot-based approaches.\n-\n-### Requirements\n-- Node.js 18 or newer\n-- VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Desktop, Goose, Grok, Junie or any other MCP client\n-\n-<!--\n-// Generate using:\n-node utils/generate-links.js\n--->\n-\n-### Getting started\n-\n-First, install the Playwright MCP server with your client.\n-\n-**Standard config** works in
